items.title: Microsoft corrected PIM for Groups: eligible members and owners are credential-protected too, and changing those credentials needs Privileged Authentication Administrator
items.officialTitle: What is Privileged Identity Management for groups?
items.tier0Note: The article governs who may reset the credentials of members and owners of a role-assignable group, which is the write path used to elevate into Entra roles including Global Administrator.
items.fingerprint: Pull request 2049 reached entra-docs main at 16:57 UTC on 23 September 2026 and the live branch at 17:42 UTC. It widened the stated protection of role-assignable groups from active members to members and owners including eligible ones who have not activated, and it replaced the Helpdesk Administrator example in the security note with a general statement plus a new sentence naming Privileged Authentication Administrator as the least role that can change those credentials. The include file's ms.date moved from 01/31/2023 to 07/29/2026.
items.why: The previous wording left open the classic PIM-for-Groups attack: a lower-privileged admin resets the password of a user who is only an eligible member of a role-assignable group, then activates the assignment on their behalf. Microsoft now states that the credential protection already covers eligible members and owners, so that path is closed by the platform — but only for groups that were actually created as role-assignable.
items.action: Confirm that every group used to elevate into an Entra role is role-assignable (isAssignableToRole true). A group that is not gets none of this protection, and the eligible-member reset path is still open on it. No deadline is stated by Microsoft.

items.title: Two hidden Mail-Advanced permissions now name Office 365 Exchange Online as their resource application
items.officialTitleNote: Microsoft publishes no announcement for this; the change is visible only as a diff of permissions/new/provisioningInfo.json in the devx content repository.
items.reference: no MC/RM post — deployment map only
items.fingerprint: In the same 23 September sync, Mail-Advanced.ReadWrite (DelegatedWork, id f3af82f6-18e0-4a41-8dc8-a03c11854a8d) and Mail-Advanced.ReadWrite.All (Application, id e118f1da-5c1c-46cf-bff6-8858d786f46f) had their resourceAppId filled in for the first time: it moved from an empty string to 00000002-0000-0ff1-ce00-000000000000, which is Office 365 Exchange Online. Both are isHidden true and isEnabled true, and both are in this brief's inventory as documented Graph permissions.
items.why: The resource application decides which service principal the grant is recorded against. Naming Exchange Online rather than Microsoft Graph means a consent audit that reads only the Graph service principal will not see these two grants, and both are hidden and enabled, which is the combination that does not raise a consent prompt anyone reads.
items.action: When auditing mail-read consent, query the Office 365 Exchange Online service principal (00000002-0000-0ff1-ce00-000000000000) as well as the Graph one, and look for the two appRole ids above.

Neither name is enabled in the map, so nothing can be granted under either spelling today.

items.tier0Note: Interactive domain sign-in fails on affected Windows 11 devices because the machine secure channel with on-premises Active Directory breaks.
items.title: September update makes Windows 11 honour Machine Identity Isolation; devices not on a Windows Server 2025 domain functional level lose domain trust
items.officialTitle: Domain-joined devices might lose their secure trust relationship with the domain
items.reference: no MC/RM post — Windows release health
items.fingerprint: Opened 16 September 2026 (status Mitigated): after KB5124008 (24H2/25H2) or KB5124012 (26H1) and later updates, Windows begins honouring existing or policy-provisioned Machine Identity Isolation enforcement. The feature is supported only with domain controllers at Windows Server 2025 domain functional level; elsewhere Credential Guard protected machine accounts can lose their secure channel and users cannot sign in with valid domain credentials. Cached sign-in may still work; AD replication is not affected. Workaround: set MachineIdentityIsolation to 0 by the method that enabled it, restart, then run Test-ComputerSecureChannel -Repair. Microsoft plans to temporarily block enforcement in a future update.
items.why: A help-desk wave of 'trust relationship failed' sign-in errors after Patch Tuesday is this known issue, not an attack — but only if Machine Identity Isolation was enabled somewhere.
items.action: Find every Intune or Group Policy setting that enables Machine Identity Isolation; unless all DCs run Windows Server 2025 DFL, set it to 0 and repair the secure channel.

items.title: Entra Connect Sync 2.6.91.0 ships security fixes; Microsoft says upgrade as soon as possible
items.officialTitleNote: Microsoft publishes this release as a version heading in the Entra Connect version history, not as a headline; the heading is copied character for character from MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs at 79a7b4c617 (merged 16 September 2026, 14:21 UTC).
items.fingerprint: Released for download on 16 September 2026 through the Entra admin center. Microsoft: "This release includes security fixes. We recommend upgrading to this version as soon as possible." It makes phishing-resistant sign-in in the setup wizard generally available and on by default, adds a guided migration to Cloud Sync, fixes an Application-Based Authentication certificate rotation issue that could remove the last usable application key, and adds Microsoft Graph permissions to Connect. Version 2.6.84.0 now retires on 16 September 2027.

Microsoft also warns that the release adds Graph permissions to Connect, so app-scoped Conditional Access policies aimed at Microsoft.Azure.SyncFabric or Microsoft 365 Reporting Service need a review before the upgrade.
items.why: Security fixes on the sync server, and new Graph permissions that app-scoped Conditional Access can block.
items.action: Schedule the upgrade to 2.6.91.0; review app-scoped CA policies targeting Microsoft.Azure.SyncFabric or Microsoft 365 Reporting Service first.

items.officialTitle: Enable local admin setting in Cloud PC configurations now in Public Preview

items.title: Copilot spending policies auto-cover new services and agents by default; AI Reader and Global Reader gain consumption dashboards
items.fingerprint: Copilot Credits spending policies gain an 'Auto-apply new services' setting that is on by default, so newly released pay-as-you-go Copilot services and agents inherit policy coverage automatically. Consumption dashboards open to AI Reader, Global Reader and License Administrator, and custom approval routing arrives for Cowork credit requests. Rollout starts early September 2026.
items.officialTitle: Microsoft Copilot Cost Management: September Updates

items.title: Legacy Whiteboard migration tooling retires 25 Sep; unmigrated boards are deleted 16 Oct
items.fingerprint: Reissue of retracted MC1469559: legacy Azure-backed Whiteboards must be migrated to OneDrive storage before migration tooling retires on 25 September 2026; they turn read-only until 16 October 2026, are then permanently deleted, and the legacy service shuts down on 30 November 2026.
items.officialTitle: [Whiteboard] Legacy Whiteboard migration to OneDrive

items.title: 30-day reminder: Windows Server 2022 mainstream support ends 13 Oct 2026
items.officialTitle: 30-Day Reminder: Windows Server 2022 will reach end of mainstream support on October 13, 2026
items.fingerprint: On October 13, 2026, Windows Server 2022 will reach end of mainstream support. The October 2026 security update will be the last mainstream support update available for this version; security updates continue through October 14, 2031, and Hotpatch for Datacenter: Azure Edition is extended through October 2027.

items.title: Container Apps Operator and Jobs Operator roles can read secret values in plain text
items.officialTitle: Permissions for managing secrets
items.fingerprint: Microsoft now documents that listSecrets returns Container Apps, jobs and Dapr component secret values in plain text, and that Container Apps Contributor, Container Apps Operator, Container Apps Jobs Contributor, Container Apps Jobs Operator, ManagedEnvironments Contributor and ConnectedEnvironments Contributor grant it through wildcard actions, even where the role description suggests narrower operational access.

items.title: Azure RBAC role assignment limit per subscription rises from 4,000 to 5,000
items.officialTitle: Troubleshoot Azure RBAC limits
items.fingerprint: Azure supports up to 5000 role assignments per subscription (previously 4000); the limit is fixed and cannot be increased; eligible and future-scheduled assignments do not count; the management-group limit stays at 500.

items.title: Defender for Cloud retires the grouped 'vulnerability assessment solution' recommendation on 11 Oct 2026
items.officialTitle: Upcoming deprecation of the Machines should have a vulnerability assessment solution recommendation
items.fingerprint: As part of the transition to individual recommendations, the Machines should have a vulnerability assessment solution recommendation will be deprecated on October 11, 2026; coverage is tracked through individual recommendations instead.

items.title: Insider Risk Management retires the 'Alerts (classic)' tab on 1 Oct 2026 for the unified alert queue
items.officialTitle: Microsoft Purview: Insider Risk Management - Unified alert queue
items.fingerprint: Updated September 10, 2026: global rollout of the unified alert queue begins early October and completes mid-October 2026; the 'Alerts (classic)' tab will be deprecated for commercial clouds on October 1 and Government clouds as of October 31; Alert Spotlight is being retired.

items.title: My Staff access now follows admin role assignment alone; the 'Administrators can access My Staff' toggle no longer does anything
items.officialTitle: Manage your users with My Staff
items.fingerprint: Access to My Staff is determined by administrative role assignment and its administrative-unit scope; the legacy My Apps and My Staff experience settings, such as Administrators can access My Staff, are no longer used by the service and are being removed from the admin center.

items.title: Legacy Apple software-update commands are removed from Intune
items.officialTitle: Plan for Change: Removal of legacy Apple MDM software updates
items.fingerprint: Microsoft is removing the legacy Apple MDM software-update commands from Intune; macOS and iOS/iPadOS patch enforcement must move to declarative device management.

items.tier0Note: Intune administrative authorisation changes shape: an admin who today holds two role assignments with different scope tags stops getting the union of them. Effective access can shrink silently for the people who run device security policy.
items.title: Scoped permissions become the default for every Intune tenant, and permissions stop merging across scope tags
items.officialTitle: Scoped permissions for role-based access control moving to general availability
items.fingerprint: At GA, Scoped permissions is the default behaviour for all tenants and Intune no longer merges permissions across role assignments that share a permission category but use different scope tags; Microsoft points administrators at Tenant administration > Roles > Settings > Permissions Assessment Report.

items.title: Windows devices can be marked non-compliant when a prohibited local AI agent is found
items.officialTitle: Mark Windows devices noncompliant when prohibited AI agents are discovered
items.fingerprint: An Intune compliance policy setting will detect locally installed AI agents (Microsoft names OpenClaw) and mark the device non-compliant, which Conditional Access can then act on.

items.title: Intune Device control policy will start applying to MDE-managed devices that were never enrolled
items.officialTitle: Support for Intune Device control policy for devices managed by Microsoft Defender for Endpoint
items.fingerprint: Existing Intune Device control policies will begin applying to devices that are attached through Defender for Endpoint security settings management rather than enrolled in Intune, so current assignment scope reaches a wider fleet than it did when written.

items.tier0Note: A non-human principal that writes device configuration policy is a new privileged identity in the tenant, and it will not appear in any review built around human admins.
items.title: The Policy Configuration Agent moves off a human identity onto an Entra agentic identity
items.officialTitle: Agentic identity for the Policy Configuration Agent (public preview)
items.fingerprint: The Intune Policy Configuration Agent will act under a Microsoft Entra agentic identity instead of the signed-in administrator's identity.

items.title: macOS 14 and iOS/iPadOS 17 will stop being enrollable once Apple ships version 27
items.officialTitle: Updated minimum supported version for macOS
items.deadlineNote: Microsoft ties the change to Apple's release of macOS 27 and iOS/iPadOS 27 and states no calendar date.
items.fingerprint: After Apple releases macOS 27 and iOS/iPadOS 27, Intune raises its minimum supported versions and devices on macOS 14 or iOS/iPadOS 17 can no longer enroll.

items.title: Teams and Outlook launch failures on ARM devices are fixed by KB5124008
items.officialTitle: Teams and Outlook fail to launch on ARM-based devices
items.reference: no MC/RM post — Windows release health
items.fingerprint: The Windows 11 25H2 known issue opened on 1 September 2026 where Teams and Outlook fail to launch on ARM-based devices was resolved on 8 September 2026 by KB5124008.

items.officialTitle: Windows 11 Enterprise and Education, Version 23H2

items.title: .NET 8 LTS and PowerShell 7.4 LTS end servicing on 10 November 2026 — the runtimes most SOC automation stands on
items.officialTitle: .NET 8 (LTS)
items.publishedNote: Microsoft prints no publication date for a lifecycle row; the page was last updated 19 August 2026.

items.officialTitle: Azure Functions In-process model end of support
items.publishedNote: Microsoft prints no publication date for a lifecycle row; the page was last updated 19 August 2026.

items.title: Azure Maps Render V1 and Web SDK v1 map controls retire mid-September
items.officialTitle: Azure Maps Render V1
items.publishedNote: Microsoft prints no publication date for a lifecycle row; the page was last updated 19 August 2026.

items.title: Anomaly Detector, Metrics Advisor and Personalizer retire on 1 October 2026
items.officialTitle: Azure Anomaly Detector
items.publishedNote: Microsoft prints no publication date for a lifecycle row; the page was last updated 19 August 2026.
items.fingerprint: Azure Anomaly Detector, Azure Metrics Advisor and Azure Personalizer retire on 1 October 2026, along with the Translator billing model change.

items.title: Display Protection reaches Windows 365 and Azure Virtual Desktop in preview
items.officialTitle: Display Protection for Windows 365 (Public Preview)
items.fingerprint: Display Protection secures the display path between a Cloud PC and the endpoint, configurable from Intune, with the matching Azure Virtual Desktop preview configured per host pool in the Azure portal.

items.title: Researchers publish fresh bypasses for the patched Defender ShieldBreak flaw
items.officialTitle: Researcher Drops New Microsoft Defender PoC Showing ShieldBreak Patch Can Be Bypassed
items.reference: third-party reporting — no Microsoft advisory found at time of reading
items.fingerprint: The Hacker News and Petri report a new proof of concept showing the patch for the Microsoft Defender ShieldBreak flaw can be bypassed by exploit variants; Microsoft has published no advisory this brief could find.

items.title: September Windows Server updates are reported to break Remote Desktop Services
items.officialTitle: September Windows Server updates break Remote Desktop Services
items.reference: third-party reporting — not present on Windows release health at time of reading
items.fingerprint: BleepingComputer reports that the September 2026 Windows Server cumulative updates break Remote Desktop Services; this brief found no matching entry on Windows release health when it read that page on 12 September 2026.

items.title: Infostealer logs are carrying replayable AI-service tokens that sidestep MFA
items.officialTitle: Infostealer Logs Expose Replayable AI Tokens That Can Bypass MFA
items.reference: third-party reporting — no Microsoft advisory found at time of reading
items.fingerprint: Tokens harvested by infostealers and traded in logs can be replayed against AI services without re-authentication, so MFA on the account does not stop reuse of the stolen session.

items.title: Risk export guidance separates diagnostic categories from the KQL table names
items.officialTitle: Diagnostic setting categories vs Log Analytics table names
items.fingerprint: Microsoft added a mapping table stating that the six ID Protection diagnostic setting categories are not the table names a KQL query uses: RiskyUsers exports into AADRiskyUsers, UserRiskEvents into AADUserRiskEvents, RiskyServicePrincipals into AADRiskyServicePrincipals, ServicePrincipalRiskEvents into AADServicePrincipalRiskEvents, RiskyAgents into AADRiskyAgents and AgentRiskEvents into AADAgentRiskEvents. A hunting query written against the category name returns nothing and raises no error.
items.backfillNote: Microsoft committed the edit on 10 September 2026 and it reached the public branch in the 11 September merge that this brief already had at HEAD 8ec74d1. The 06:40 pass carried neither the article nor the mapping; the 21:10 re-check found it through daily.entra.news and confirmed it on the Learn page itself.
items.publishedNote: The date is the one on Microsoft's own commit to the article, not the date this brief saw it. The article itself is older.
items.revisionNote: Commit 526695a, "Map ID Protection diagnostic categories to Log Analytics tables", 10 September 2026.

items.title: Teams real-time alerting rules gain duplication, bulk user upload and direct deletion
items.officialTitle: Microsoft Teams: Enhanced real-time alerting rule management in the Teams admin center
items.fingerprint: Rule duplication, bulk user upload and direct deletion arrive in the Teams admin center under Notifications & alerts > Rules, and one tenant can monitor up to 500 users across its In-Progress Meetings and Calls rules. The capability is on by default from late September 2026, so an alerting rule set can be copied and widened without anyone enabling anything first.
items.backfillNote: Published 12 September at 00:43 UTC, inside the window and four hours before the 06:40 pass, which did not carry it and did not record it as dropped.

items.title: Azure Linux with OS Guard support in AKS ends
items.officialTitle: Retirement: Azure Linux with OS Guard in Azure Kubernetes Service
items.fingerprint: Microsoft states that support for Azure Linux with OS Guard in Azure Kubernetes Service ends on 10 December 2026. OS Guard is the hardened, integrity-enforced variant of the node image, so a cluster left on it after that date runs an unsupported host-hardening configuration.

items.title: Storage Mover can copy on-premises SMB shares into Azure Files with no agent on the file server
items.officialTitle: Public Preview: Agentless migration of on-premises SMB file shares to Azure Files (SMB)
items.fingerprint: Azure Storage Mover gains a preview path that reads an on-premises SMB share into Azure Files without an agent installed on the file server, which moves file data across the network boundary through a service-side connection rather than a host this organisation runs.

items.title: Endpoint DLP changes how it classifies archive files on Windows
items.officialTitle: Microsoft Purview: Endpoint Data Loss Prevention-Archive File Classification Behavior Change for Windows Endpoints
items.fingerprint: Roadmap 570965, created 9 September 2026: Endpoint DLP on Windows changes its archive-file classification behaviour, which alters which ZIP and container contents are inspected and therefore which existing endpoint DLP rules fire.
items.why: A classification behaviour change is a silent detection change: rules that matched yesterday may not match tomorrow, and the reverse.
items.action: Baseline current Endpoint DLP match volume on archive files now, so the before-and-after is measurable when this ships.

items.title: Purview DLP extends to Microsoft Cowork
items.officialTitle: Microsoft Purview: Data Loss Prevention for Microsoft Cowork
items.fingerprint: Roadmap 570845, created 8 September 2026: Purview Data Loss Prevention gains coverage of Microsoft Cowork, a surface that until now had no DLP policy enforcement of its own.
items.why: A new agentic surface reaching tenant data without DLP coverage is an exfiltration path; this closes it, but only for tenants that write the policy.
items.action: Add Cowork to the DLP policy scoping review when it reaches preview; an uncovered surface is not covered by a policy that never names it.

items.title: Unauthenticated wormable DNS Server RCE ships in the September 2026 update
items.reference: no MC/RM post — MSRC vulnerability page; wormability and CVSS are third-party characterisations
items.fingerprint: CVE-2026-69730 is a use-after-free in Windows DNS Server reachable without authentication. Microsoft does not mark it exploited. Third-party trackers (Tenable, CrowdStrike, Help Net Security) score it CVSS 9.8, count it among roughly twenty unauthenticated wormable bugs in this release and compare it to SIGRed; Microsoft publishes no wormability statement of its own.
items.tier0Note: DNS Server runs on domain controllers in the overwhelming majority of Active Directory deployments, so an unauthenticated remote code execution path in it is a Tier 0 path by placement rather than by privilege.
items.urgencyNote: Not marked exploited by Microsoft, but it is remote, pre-authentication and sits on domain controllers — patch alongside the two exploited elevation-of-privilege flaws, not after them.
items.why: An unauthenticated remote code execution bug in a service that almost always runs on a domain controller collapses the distance between the network perimeter and Tier 0.

items.title: Azure AD B2C elevation of privilege carries the highest score in the September 2026 release
items.reference: no MC/RM post — MSRC vulnerability page; CVSS reported by third-party trackers
items.fingerprint: CVE-2026-83711 is an elevation-of-privilege flaw in Azure Active Directory B2C, rated Critical. The Zero Day Initiative and BleepingComputer both report CVSS 10.0, the highest score in the September 2026 release; Microsoft's own severity is Critical and the service-side fix requires no customer action.
items.tier0Note: B2C tenants issue tokens to external consumers, and an elevation of privilege inside that issuer reaches every relying application that trusts it.
items.urgencyNote: Service-side fix. The action is to confirm whether the tenant runs B2C at all and to review its sign-in telemetry for the week before the fix, not to deploy anything.
items.why: The highest-scored bug of a record Patch Tuesday sits in an identity issuer, and a SOC that only tracks Windows CVEs will not have seen it.

items.title: AgentIdentity.ReadWrite.All can now PATCH any service principal, not only an agent identity
items.fingerprint: Microsoft's weekly permissions sync moved PATCH off the agent-identity-only path and onto the generic /serviceprincipals/{id}. An application already holding this admin-consented, privilegeLevel 3 scope can now modify every service principal object in the tenant. The permission name did not change, so no fresh consent prompt fires and nothing in the audit trail marks the moment.
items.officialTitle: Read and write all agent identities
items.tier0Note: A write path onto every service principal object reaches the app registrations that carry GA-equivalent Graph application roles, so an app with this scope can alter the credentials and properties of privileged service principals.
items.why: This is the shape of change that leaves no trace: the consent grant is unchanged, the permission name is unchanged, and the reach is wider than it was this morning.
items.action: List the applications and service principals holding AgentIdentity.ReadWrite.All (application role dcf7150a-88d4-4fe6-9be1-c2744c455397, delegated 4a4facd5-0ee1-49b7-a5b2-fdcc2491685e) and decide whether each still warrants write access to every service principal.

items.title: Cloud Sync configuration article drops the note naming the sync service account and its MFA trap
items.fingerprint: Microsoft removed the NOTE that named the provisioning service account created during configuration, ADToAADSyncServiceAccount@[TenantID].onmicrosoft.com, and warned that multifactor authentication or any interactive authentication policy on that account breaks configuration. The article no longer tells a reader the account exists or how a tenant-wide Conditional Access policy will break provisioning.
items.officialTitle: Removed obsolete sync account creation note
items.tier0Note: The Cloud Sync provisioning account writes into Active Directory; the removed note was the only place the configuration article named it and said what authentication policy breaks it.
items.why: A Conditional Access policy scoped to all users still breaks Cloud Sync; the article that used to warn about it no longer does, and the account name a SOC would exclude or monitor is gone with it.
items.action: Keep the exclusion or monitoring you have for ADToAADSyncServiceAccount@<tenant>.onmicrosoft.com; do not treat the note's removal as evidence the constraint was lifted.

items.title: Entra Kerberos hybrid join drops EnableKerbHaadj.exe for a Windows Server 2025 build floor
items.fingerprint: The remediation for DSREG_TOKEN_MISSING_ON_PREM_ID and SEC_E_NO_AUTHENTICATING_AUTHORITY changed from running the private-preview tool EnableKerbHaadj.exe on every Windows Server 2025 domain controller to requiring those domain controllers to run build 26100.6905 (KB5070881) or later.
items.officialTitle: Remove private preview instructions from the file
items.tier0Note: The instruction applies to every Windows Server 2025 domain controller in the Active Directory domain.
items.why: A documented remediation that told administrators to run an unsigned preview tool on domain controllers is gone.
items.action: Where EnableKerbHaadj.exe was run on a domain controller, move that host to build 26100.6905 or later instead.

items.title: Global Secure Access health articles now name the licences, roles and Graph permissions each signal needs
items.fingerprint: Three scenario-health articles gained a prerequisites block: Reports Reader is the least privileged role for viewing signals, alerts and alert configurations; Helpdesk Administrator the least privileged role for updating them; HealthMonitoringAlert.Read.All and HealthMonitoringAlert.ReadWrite.All are the Graph permissions for reading and modifying alerts; viewing alerts also needs a non-trial Entra P1 or P2 licence and at least 100 monthly active users.
items.officialTitle: Improve GSA scenario health troubleshooting guidance
items.why: Until today these pages did not say which role or Graph permission a reader needs, so access was granted by guesswork.
items.action: Re-scope whoever holds Global Secure Access health access to Reports Reader, or Helpdesk Administrator where they must update alerts.

items.title: The Entra health alerts how-to moved from howto-use to howto-investigate
items.fingerprint: MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs carries a redirection from docs/identity/monitoring-health/howto-use-health-scenario-alerts.md to /entra/identity/monitoring-health/howto-investigate-health-scenario-alerts, and the three scenario articles were rewritten to point at the new address.
items.officialTitleNote: Microsoft published no headline for a redirection; the move is recorded in .openpublishing.redirection.json, not in an article title.
items.why: A bookmark or runbook pointing at the old address now depends on a redirect rather than on a page.
items.action: Update any runbook that links howto-use-health-scenario-alerts to the howto-investigate address.

items.title: App Gallery self-service onboarding will not validate an application on identity platform v1 endpoints
items.fingerprint: A new section states that self-service Microsoft Entra App Gallery onboarding supports only Microsoft identity platform v2 OpenID Connect endpoints, and that applications on v1 endpoints cannot be validated through the self-service experience. Microsoft recommends migrating to v2, whose scope-based model supports incremental consent.
items.officialTitle: Microsoft identity platform v1 endpoints aren't supported
items.why: Any in-flight gallery submission built on a v1 endpoint is now documented as unable to pass validation.
items.action: Check whether any application queued for gallery publication still uses a v1 endpoint, and plan the v2 migration before submitting.

items.title: Access package resource roles gain a documented search box for SharePoint sites with many roles
items.fingerprint: Both access-package articles gained the same sentence: for SharePoint Online sites with a large number of roles, the search box returns matching roles even when the list does not initially display all of them.
items.officialTitle: Update access package docs with SharePoint site role search guidance
items.why: A role that the picker did not display was previously indistinguishable from a role that does not exist.
items.action: No action. Note it when an access package appears to be missing a SharePoint role.

items.title: Primary refresh token troubleshooting corrects the Start-auth.ps1 switch to -vAuth
items.fingerprint: The documented command changed from .\Start-auth.ps1 -v -acceptEULA to .\Start-auth.ps1 -vAuth -acceptEULA.
items.officialTitle: Fix PowerShell command for starting auth script.
items.why: The published switch did not exist, so anyone following the article verbatim collected no trace.
items.action: Use -vAuth when collecting a primary refresh token trace.

items.title: Multi-account support for Sentinel codeless connectors enters public preview
items.fingerprint: The Microsoft Sentinel blog announced public preview of multi-account support for codeless connectors, letting one connector definition collect from several accounts of the same source.
items.officialTitle: Public Preview: Multi-account support for Microsoft Sentinel codeless connectors
items.why: One connector per account is the reason several tenants run duplicated codeless connectors today.
items.action: If you run duplicate codeless connectors per account, review whether the preview collapses them.

items.tier0Note: The out-of-band rollup covers Windows Server 2012 through 2025, so it lands on domain controllers and other Tier 0 servers; on 26H1, 25H2 and 24H2 it is itself a security update.
items.title: Out-of-band Windows update fixes RDS hangs from the September rollup and patches CVE-2026-62721
items.officialTitle: Take Action: Out-of-band update released to address issues from the September 2026 Windows security update
items.fingerprint: On 14 September 2026 Microsoft released out-of-band updates for issues caused by the 8 September security update: Remote Desktop Services might stop responding and block local and remote sign-in, Hyper-V Linux guests can lose host folder shares, and some USB Audio Class 1.0 devices fail. For Windows 11 26H1, 25H2 and 24H2 the update is a security update that also fixes CVE-2026-62721 (26H1 also CVE-2026-85921); KB5129195 covers 25H2/24H2, KB5129235 Server 2025, KB5129237 Server 2022.
items.why: A server that stops accepting RDP or local sign-in after Patch Tuesday looks like an outage or an attack; the fix is also a security update on current Windows 11 builds.
items.action: Deploy the out-of-band KBs to RDS hosts and servers that took the September rollup, and confirm CVE-2026-62721 coverage on Windows 11 26H1, 25H2 and 24H2.

items.title: Conditional Access now applies to Outlook attachment download, preview and upload
items.officialTitle: (Updated) Enhanced security and access controls for Outlook attachments
items.fingerprint: Outlook attachments run under a separate internal application configuration that inherits the Conditional Access policies assigned to the Exchange and Office cloud apps; users who fail a policy cannot download, preview or upload classic attachments, including inline images. Available now. Continuous Access Evaluation is not yet supported for this configuration. Microsoft revised the post at 16:32 UTC on 23 September 2026 and reversed its own statement about scoping: attachment-only Conditional Access policies are supported after all, through a first-party application named OwaDownloadAttachments, appId e4f2bb2d-a4d0-4eab-aac6-a8b83471cf64, for which a service principal must first be created in the tenant.
items.why: Two things changed for a SOC. An exclusion you already made for Exchange Online does not carry over to attachments, so a user who can reach mail can still be blocked from downloading, previewing or uploading an attachment, and that will arrive as a help-desk ticket rather than as a policy change. And a new first-party application id now appears as a Conditional Access target resource, which is a name your policy review has never seen.
items.action: Re-read every Conditional Access policy that excludes Exchange Online and decide whether attachments should be excluded too. To scope attachments separately, create the service principal for appId e4f2bb2d-a4d0-4eab-aac6-a8b83471cf64 once (Cloud Application Administrator or Global Administrator, consent to Application.ReadWrite.All), then exclude or target OwaDownloadAttachments per policy.

items.title: Admins get a control over who can upload advanced agents and plugins; uploads stay open by default from 25 Oct
items.officialTitle: Manage who can upload advanced agents and plugins
items.deadlineNote: 25 October 2026 is when advanced-package uploads become enabled by default unless an admin has chosen no users or specific users or groups.
items.fingerprint: From 25 September 2026 the Microsoft 365 admin center shows an Advanced package uploads setting under Copilot settings (all users, no users, or specific users or Entra ID groups). An advanced package is a declarative agent with actions or with an MCP server. Starting 25 October 2026 advanced-package uploads are enabled by default unless the admin has restricted them. Updated 15 September 2026.
items.why: User-uploaded agents with actions or MCP servers can reach data and external endpoints; the default after 25 October is open.
items.action: Decide before 25 October 2026 who may upload advanced agents and plugins, and scope the setting to an Entra ID group if not all users.

items.title: B2B passkey rollout: guests enabled for SMS or voice will be auto-enabled for all passkey types
items.officialTitle: (Updated) Microsoft Entra ID: Passkey support for B2B users
items.publishedNote: First posted 21 August 2026; revised by Microsoft on 14 September 2026, which is the date carried here.
items.fingerprint: Revised 14 September 2026: B2B users (internal guests and external users) who are enabled for SMS or voice in the Authentication methods policy or legacy MFA policies will be automatically enabled for all passkey types under the SMS/voice retirement changes (MC1426371, MC1434201); excluding them only from the passkey policy does not prevent it. Internal guest rollout begins early October 2026 and completes late October; external users later.
items.why: Guests can start registering resource-tenant passkeys even where the passkey policy excludes them, if they remain enabled for SMS or voice.
items.action: Review SMS and voice assignments for guest and external users in both the Authentication methods policy and legacy MFA settings before early October.
items.dateNote: First published by Microsoft on 21 Aug 2026; the 14 Sep 2026 shown is the later revision or rollout date that puts this row in the 2-16 September window.

items.title: Purview DLP starts evaluating calendar events in Outlook for Mac and Outlook Mobile
items.officialTitle: [Outlook Mac] Purview Data Loss Prevention support for Calendar Events
items.fingerprint: Microsoft announced Purview Data Loss Prevention support for calendar events in Outlook for Mac (MC1472022) and Outlook Mobile (MC1472023), extending DLP policy evaluation to meeting content created on those clients.
items.why: DLP alerts can start arriving from calendar events created on Mac and mobile clients.
items.action: Check which DLP policies target Exchange so calendar-event matches do not surprise the alert queue.

items.title: Purview DLP wait-on-send reaches Outlook for Mac and Outlook Mobile
items.officialTitle: [Outlook Mac] Purview DLP Wait-on-Send Support
items.fingerprint: Microsoft announced Purview DLP wait-on-send support for Outlook for Mac (MC1472019) and Outlook Mobile (MC1472021), so a message is held while DLP policies are evaluated before it is sent.
items.why: Closes a gap where Mac and mobile clients could send before a DLP verdict.
items.action: No action stated by Microsoft; note it for DLP coverage reviews.

items.title: Microsoft starts automatically onboarding MSSP-managed Sentinel customers to the Defender portal
items.officialTitle: Automatic onboarding for Microsoft Sentinel
items.reference: no MC/RM post — Partner Center announcement
items.fingerprint: Starting September 2026 Microsoft automatically onboards managed customers that have not moved to the unified Sentinel experience in the Defender portal; admins get a banner and email about 30 days before. Microsoft selects one primary workspace for Defender XDR alerts and incidents, and XDR-dependent content in secondary workspaces might stop working.
items.why: Analytics rules, automation rules and playbooks in a secondary workspace can silently stop working once Microsoft picks the primary.
items.action: For multi-workspace managed tenants, migrate XDR-dependent rules and playbooks to the intended primary workspace, or email MSSP-Sentinel-Support@microsoft.com to request a different primary.

items.officialTitleNote: Microsoft prints this as a note on the Sentinel data lake onboarding page, without a headline of its own.
items.title: Purview data risk graph deprecated: configuration ends 30 September in Data Security Investigations, retired 24 November in Insider Risk Management
items.publishedNote: Microsoft prints no publication date for this note.
items.deadlineNote: 30 Sep 2026 ends configuration of Data risk graph in Data Security Investigations; full retirement 30 Nov 2026 in DSI. In Insider Risk Management Microsoft prints one date only: retirement on 24 Nov 2026, with no onboarding cut-off.
items.fingerprint: Microsoft's Data Security Investigations page states that beginning 30 September 2026 organizations can no longer configure Data risk graph and that it is fully retired after 30 November 2026. Microsoft's Insider Risk Management page states that the data risk graph in Insider Risk Management will be retired on 24 November 2026 and gives no earlier configuration cut-off.
items.why: Insider-risk investigations that rely on the data risk graph lose it by late November.
items.action: Move insider-exfiltration correlation off the data risk graph before 24 November 2026; stop planning new Data Security Investigations configurations after 30 September 2026.

items.title: Registration campaign in the Enabled state now prompts Authenticator setup after any MFA method, not only SMS or voice
items.officialTitle: Clarify registration campaign MFA requirements
items.fingerprint: Microsoft rewrote the eligibility table on 15 September 2026: the MFA requirement now depends on campaign state. In the Microsoft managed state an Authenticator campaign still prompts only after SMS or voice MFA, but in the Enabled state it prompts after MFA with any method, and the eligible-users row changed from users who sign in by voice call or SMS to users who sign in by using any MFA method.
items.why: Tenants that switched the campaign to Enabled will see Authenticator nudges reach users who already use stronger methods.
items.action: Check the campaign state and targeting before users on passkeys or Authenticator start receiving prompts.

items.title: Identity Security dashboard and Coverage & Maturity reach general availability
items.officialTitle: Identity Security dashboard and Coverage & Maturity

items.why: Gives the SOC a supported view of identity coverage gaps across on-premises and SaaS identity providers.
items.action: Review Coverage & Maturity for unprotected identity sources and prioritise the listed setup tasks.

items.officialTitleNote: Microsoft publishes no title for this: the names are read out of the Graph service principal, which Microsoft does not document until later. The heading shown is the dump commit this brief read.
items.tier0Note: Ten scopes an application can be consented to today, one of which reads every group membership in the tenant and two of which rewrite the rules governing access to protected content.
items.why: Two of them stand out. GroupMember.ReadBasic.All reads every group membership in the organisation as an application, with no signed-in user — that is the whole org chart and the membership of every privileged access group, in one call. And InfoProtectABACPolicy.ReadWrite.All plus InfoProtectAttributeAssignment.ReadWrite.All together let a holder define an attribute, assign it to a principal and thereby grant access to protected content without touching a group, a role or a label.
items.action: Put all ten appRoleIds on the consent-alert list today, ahead of the documentation. The two that matter most are 8222c640-cae5-4860-8d11-b32cfad95e03 (GroupMember.ReadBasic.All) and 4bfc1735-3a0c-4602-a159-9cfa07213339 (InfoProtectABACPolicy.ReadWrite.All). Then ask Purview whether an ABAC policy catalog is being enabled in this tenant, because nothing else has announced it.
items.title: Ten new Graph permissions become grantable in the service principal — six of them a brand-new Purview ABAC surface, none documented
items.officialTitle: _info/GraphAppRoles.json and _info/GraphDelegateRoles.json — Daily automation, commit 80698c1

items.fingerprint: Between the 13 and the 17 September 2026 dumps of the Microsoft Graph service principal, application roles went from 731 to 741 and delegated scopes from 815 to 825, with nothing removed. The ten new names are CaseManagement.ConfigManage.All, Group-PreferredDataLocation.ReadWrite.All, Group.ReadBasic.All, GroupMember.ReadBasic.All and six InfoProtect* scopes covering the ABAC policy catalog, attribute definitions and attribute assignments. All ten are enabled and admin-consentable; none appears on Microsoft's permissions reference, which has not moved since 4 August 2026.

items.officialTitleNote: Microsoft publishes no prose title for this file; the heading shown is the commit that carried the change.
items.tier0Note: Adds a consent surface over Defender playbook execution — the exact capability an attacker wants after compromising an app registration.
items.why: The same resource app already carries AutomationRules, PlaybookEditor and SecurityIncidentTask scopes. Read and write over playbook EXECUTIONS is the step from editing automation to running it, and it is arriving without documentation or a consent page.
items.action: Add the four names to the app-consent watchlist now, before they become grantable. Nothing can consent to them today; the point is to notice the first tenant that can.

items.fingerprint: AutomationIntegrations.Read.All, AutomationIntegrations.ReadWrite.All, AutomationPlaybookExecutions.Read.All and AutomationPlaybookExecutions.ReadWrite.All appear in Microsoft's own deployment map on 17 September 2026 against resource app fc780465-2017-40d4-a0c5-307022471b92, the Defender security-automation surface, all four isHidden true and isEnabled false in the public ring; none is documented on the permissions reference.

items.tier0Note: An already-consented detection-engineering permission reaches further with no new consent prompt.
items.why: Saved hunting queries are detection logic. An app consented months ago to run ad-hoc hunts can now enumerate the SOC's own query library — coverage, blind spots and all — and no consent event fires to mark the moment.
items.action: Enumerate every service principal holding ThreatHunting.Read.All and decide whether each one should be able to read the saved query library. Treat GET /security/threathunting/queries as a new audit-worthy call.

items.officialTitle: ThreatHunting.Read.All — Run hunting queries and read saved hunting queries
items.reference: no MC/RM post — Microsoft permission data only
items.fingerprint: Microsoft's permissions.json changed the consent text of ThreatHunting.Read.All from "Run hunting queries" to "Run hunting queries and read saved hunting queries" and added GET /security/threathunting/queries and GET /security/threathunting/queries/{id} to both the delegated and application schemes.

items.tier0Note: A new custom-extension hook in the sign-in path — code Microsoft will call during account-takeover evaluation.
items.why: Custom authentication extensions run outbound HTTP from Entra at authentication time. A new extension point in the account-takeover path is a new place to put code — and a new place an attacker with EventListener.ReadWrite.All can point Entra at their own endpoint.
items.action: Baseline /identity/authenticationEventListeners today so the first onAccountTakeoverProtectionStart listener that appears in the tenant is visibly new. Review who holds EventListener.ReadWrite.All.

items.why: Anything built against the preview accessOrchestratorRequests surface stops working, and access-request automation failing silently is an access-governance gap, not just a broken script.
items.action: Search internal tooling for accessOrchestratorRequests and move it to dynamicAccessSessions. Confirm the new POST .../submit path is covered by the same approval logging you relied on before.

items.tier0Note: Narrows a Graph permission that thousands of apps hold, to close a security vulnerability, while the change is already rolling.
items.deadlineNote: (inferred) Microsoft states rollout begins mid-September 2026 and is expected to complete by late September 2026; 30 September 2026 is this brief's reading of "late September".
items.why: User.ReadBasic.All is the permission people grant when they want an app to read nothing sensitive. It has been returning appRoleAssignments — effectively who holds which application role — to every app that asked. Apps break this month; the exposure existed until now.
items.action: In Entra admin center > Enterprise applications > Permissions, list every app granted User.ReadBasic.All, and for each one ask both questions: will it break, and did it ever read appRoleAssignments it should not have. Move the legitimate ones to User.Read.All or LicenseAssignment.Read.All and re-consent.
items.title: User.ReadBasic.All stops returning app role assignments and licence details — a security fix, live this month
items.officialTitle: Microsoft Graph: User.ReadBasic.All will no longer allow reading user app role assignments and license details
items.fingerprint: Microsoft is removing access to user app role assignments and user licence details from the delegated and application permission User.ReadBasic.All to fix a security vulnerability; apps needing that data must move to User.Read.All or LicenseAssignment.Read.All. GA worldwide from mid-September 2026, expected complete late September 2026.

items.tier0Note: Automatic remediation of the AD FS token-signing key container — the Golden SAML target — on every supported server that does not opt out.
items.deadlineNote: Microsoft states enforcement begins with the October 2026 Windows security update; 13 October 2026 is that update's release date.
items.why: The DKM container holds the key material behind AD FS token signing. A loose ACL there is the Golden SAML precondition. Microsoft is about to fix it for you, which is good — and to change permissions on a domain object under your federation service without asking, which needs a maintenance window.
items.action: Install the July 2026 or later Windows update on every AD FS server, then read the AD FS Admin log for Event ID 1132 and fix what it names before 13 October. Windows Server 2012 and 2012 R2 get no automatic remediation — do those by hand.
items.title: AD FS DKM container ACL hardening switches from audit to enforcement with the October Windows update
items.officialTitle: 30-Day Reminder: AD FS DKM container ACL hardening begins in October 2026
items.fingerprint: From the October 2026 Windows security update, supported Windows Server versions will run remediation of insecure AD FS Distributed Key Manager container ACLs by default unless an administrator opts out, addressing the elevation-of-privilege vulnerability CVE-2026-56155. Windows Server 2012 and 2012 R2 are not remediated automatically and still need manual work.

items.deadlineNote: (inferred) Microsoft targets the migration for the end of Q1 2027; 31 March 2027 is this brief's reading of that phrase.
items.why: Falling out of compliance is not a reporting problem when Conditional Access requires a compliant device: it is a sign-in block, fleet-wide, on a date Microsoft chooses.
items.action: Allow the Azure Attestation endpoints named on the Intune endpoints page through proxies and firewalls, and confirm the allowance in a locked-down network segment rather than assuming it.

items.officialTitle: Intune: Windows Health Attestation Migration to Microsoft Azure Attestation
items.fingerprint: A second post, filed under Windows rather than Intune, repeats the Device Health Attestation to Microsoft Azure Attestation migration and states plainly that Windows 11 devices with compliance policies using BitLocker, Secure Boot or Code Integrity health settings will fall out of compliance if the Azure Attestation endpoints are unreachable.

items.deadlineNote: Microsoft states the date in the message title.
items.why: An unpatched Office build on a managed endpoint is a document-borne execution path that no Defender policy closes.
items.action: Inventory Office LTSC 2021 installs now — the same 13 October date carries Windows Server 2022 mainstream support and the Windows 11 24H2 servicing end, so one October window covers all three.

items.action: Pull the 24H2 and LTSB 2016 device counts out of Intune this week; anything still on them on 14 October is an unpatched endpoint, not a deferred upgrade.

items.fingerprint: Microsoft's 30-day reminder that Windows 11 version 24H2 and Windows 10 Enterprise LTSB 2016 stop receiving updates on 13 October 2026.

items.officialTitle: 60-Day Reminder: Windows 11, version 23H2 Enterprise and Education editions reach end of updates
items.fingerprint: Microsoft's 60-day reminder that Windows 11 version 23H2 Enterprise and Education editions reach end of updates in November 2026.

items.why: Quishing moved into Teams as soon as mail gateways started reading QR images. This is the first in-product control for it, and it is worth a detection baseline on either side of the rollout.
items.action: Note the rollout date so a fall in external-QR click telemetry is read as the control working rather than as a reporting gap.

items.officialTitle: Microsoft Teams: QR code protection for messages from external users
items.fingerprint: Microsoft Teams adds QR code protection for messages received from external users.

items.why: Disconnected and WSUS-scanned estates report compliance against the Scan Cab. A stale one makes patched machines look unpatched and unpatched machines look fine.
items.action: Re-import the updated Scan Cab wherever offline scanning is used before trusting this month's compliance numbers.

items.officialTitle: An updated version of the September 2026 Scan Cab is available

items.action: Warn the DLP triage queue before the rollout lands, and check that calendar-event matches are routed like mail matches rather than into an unread bucket.

items.why: Where a file physically lives decides whether an eDiscovery hold and an incident-response export actually reach it.
items.action: Confirm with the eDiscovery owner that archived-but-retained SharePoint content stays in scope for holds and exports.

items.officialTitle: Microsoft Purview: Auto-expanding archive capacity increases to 3 TB for eligible mailboxes
items.fingerprint: Auto-expanding archive capacity increases to 3 TB for eligible mailboxes.

items.why: A commercial blocker coming off a control usually means the control can now be turned on everywhere it was skipped.

items.officialTitle: Microsoft Purview: Removing pay-as-you-go requirements for DLP
items.fingerprint: Microsoft Purview removes pay-as-you-go billing requirements for DLP capabilities.

items.title: Purview ships auto-labeling and policy enhancements
items.officialTitle: Microsoft Purview: Auto-labeling and policy enhancements
items.fingerprint: Microsoft Purview publishes auto-labeling and policy enhancements.

items.tier0Note: Lets a low-code agent reach arbitrary external tool servers from inside the tenant.

items.officialTitle: Copilot Studio - Use MCP-compliant tools in agent workflows
items.fingerprint: Copilot Studio agents can use MCP-compliant tools inside agent workflows.

items.why: Licence boundaries have been doing access-control work by accident. Removing one widens the set of directory principals that can appear inside a business application.

items.fingerprint: Dataverse allows Entra users without a Power Platform licence to be assigned to Dataverse Activities.

items.why: The Office client is a first-stage execution surface; channel-level update availability is the number that decides how long the window stays open.
items.action: Compare the current build in Intune against the channel build published this month, rather than against the last one you recorded.

items.officialTitle: Updates available for Microsoft 365 Apps for all channels
items.fingerprint: Microsoft published the September 2026 Microsoft 365 Apps updates across all update channels.

items.why: A change of sender address on automated mail is a change to what your anti-spoofing rules and your users' pattern recognition consider normal.
items.action: Find the new sender before the first user reports it as phishing, and check it against the mail-flow rules that currently allow the old one.

items.officialTitle: Power BI subscriptions: Changes to notification delivery and sender experience
items.fingerprint: Power BI subscriptions change notification delivery and the sender experience.

items.tier0Note: On-premises Exchange is an internet-facing identity and mail surface; its security updates are the shortest path to a pre-auth compromise.
items.why: Two SU posts landing together usually means an estate somewhere skipped one. On-premises Exchange remains the single most exploited Microsoft server product; the gap between release and installation is the whole risk.
items.action: Confirm every Exchange Server in the estate is on the September 2026 SU, including any server kept only for hybrid management.

items.officialTitle: Released: September 2026 Exchange Server Security Updates
items.reference: no MC/RM post — Exchange Team blog
items.fingerprint: The Exchange Team blog published the September 2026 Exchange Server security updates on 8 September 2026, and republished the August 2026 set on the same day.

items.tier0Note: NTLM removal changes what authentication a domain accepts, and every relay and pass-the-hash detection is written against it.
items.why: Every organisation still has NTLM somewhere, and almost none knows where. An FAQ is Microsoft telling you the inventory work is now yours to do — and it is the input to a hunting query, not a reading task.
items.action: Turn on NTLM auditing on domain controllers if it is not already on, and get a per-application NTLM inventory started while fallback still exists.
items.title: Microsoft publishes an NTLM retirement FAQ
items.officialTitle: Retiring NTLM: Frequently asked questions
items.reference: no MC/RM post — Windows IT Pro blog
items.fingerprint: The Windows IT Pro blog published an NTLM retirement FAQ on 9 September 2026, consolidating Microsoft's answers on timeline, inventory and fallback behaviour.

items.tier0Note: Moves an Exchange-controlled cross-tenant data flow under Entra Cross-Tenant Access policy, changing who governs it and where it is logged.
items.why: The control moves from the Exchange admin's organisation relationships to the identity admin's Cross-Tenant Access policy. Anyone who tuned outbound data sharing in Exchange should check whether their CTA policy says the same thing — because after the move, CTA is what is enforced.
items.action: Compare the existing Exchange organisation relationships against the outbound settings in Cross-Tenant Access policy and reconcile the two before Microsoft does it for you.
items.title: Cross-tenant Free/Busy, MailTips and calendar sharing move onto Cross-Tenant Access policy
items.officialTitle: Cross-tenant Free/Busy, MailTips, and Calendar Sharing are moving to Cross-Tenant Access
items.reference: no MC/RM post — Exchange Team blog
items.fingerprint: Exchange Online is moving cross-tenant Free/Busy, MailTips and calendar sharing from organisation relationships onto Entra Cross-Tenant Access policy.

items.why: A foreign tenant deleting mail from your users' mailboxes is a data-integrity event, and a plausible anti-forensic one. Whether it is logged, and to whom, decides whether an investigation can ever reconstruct what was sent.
items.action: Decide deliberately which tenants may recall into yours, and confirm a cross-tenant recall leaves an audit record you can search.
items.title: Cross-tenant message recall arrives in Exchange Online
items.officialTitle: Cross-Tenant Message Recall in Exchange Online
items.reference: no MC/RM post — Exchange Team blog
items.fingerprint: Exchange Online gains cross-tenant message recall: trusted Microsoft 365 tenants can be allowed to recall messages already delivered to your users' mailboxes.

items.why: Fileless and in-memory payloads are how Linux server intrusions avoid on-access scanning. This closes a detection gap that hunting queries could not cover from telemetry alone.
items.action: Check the Linux MDE build in the estate against the version that carries Memory Scan, then confirm the new detections reach the same queue as the Windows ones.
items.title: Defender for Endpoint adds memory scanning on Linux
items.officialTitle: Memory scan for Linux
items.fingerprint: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint extends protection on Linux with Memory Scan, inspecting process memory rather than files alone.

items.why: WSL has been a standing blind spot: a developer workstation can run a whole Linux environment that the Windows sensor barely sees. Attackers noticed before defenders did.
items.action: Find out how many managed Windows devices have WSL enabled, then deploy the plug-in to those first.

items.fingerprint: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint extends its plug-in to WSL containers (WSLc), covering workloads that previously ran outside endpoint visibility on a managed Windows device.

items.why: The App Gallery is a trust signal: administrators pick from it precisely because somebody vetted it. Self-service onboarding changes who that somebody is, and it arrives the same fortnight Microsoft began requiring submitted SCIM validation results.
items.action: Stop treating gallery presence as vetting. Review the actual permissions a gallery application requests before consent, the same way you would for a non-gallery app.

items.officialTitle: Public preview of self-service onboarding for new Microsoft Entra App Gallery applications
items.reference: no MC/RM post — Microsoft Entra blog

items.why: Business email compromise is still the loss leader in most incident-cost tables, and synthetic voice and video have removed the tells staff were trained on.
items.action: Re-test the payment-change verification process against a voice call that sounds exactly like the CFO, because that is now the threat model.
items.title: Microsoft details AI-assisted executive impersonation and invoice fraud, and the controls that stop it
items.officialTitle: Protecting organizations from AI-assisted executive impersonation and invoice fraud

items.deadlineNote: Microsoft states the retirement begins 1 February 2027 for Worldwide and GCC; the Message Center post carries that date as its action-required date.
items.title: SMS first-factor sign-in retires for workforce tenants on 1 February 2027, worldwide and in GCC
items.officialTitle: Microsoft Entra ID: Follow-up on SMS first-factor sign-in retirement and upcoming changes
items.fingerprint: From 1 February 2027 users can no longer authenticate with a phone number and an SMS one-time passcode as a primary factor; existing SMS first-factor configurations stop being honoured, the management surface is removed from the Entra administration experiences, and sign-in attempts using a registered phone number with an SMS code are blocked. Users holding another registered method keep signing in. The retirement covers workforce tenants only and does not touch Azure AD B2C or External ID. It applies even where Choose Your Own Telephony Provider is used to keep SMS or voice as a multifactor method.
items.why: This is the first factor, not the second: a tenant that still allows SMS sign-in loses a working sign-in path on the date, not a convenience. Microsoft names passkeys, QR code authentication and FIDO2 keys as the alternatives, all of which need registration campaigns that take longer than the notice period suggests.
items.action: Run an authentication methods report for users with SMS sign-in enabled (SignInNoPassword), get them registered on a phishing-resistant method, and strip SMS first-factor dependencies out of the authentication method policy before 1 February 2027.

items.title: Advanced hunting gains a MessageContents table carrying Teams message snippets, permission-gated
items.officialTitle: Microsoft Defender for Office 365: New MessageContents table in Advanced Hunting for Microsoft Teams messages
items.fingerprint: A MessageContents table becomes available in Advanced Hunting from late September 2026, completing by mid-October 2026, holding Teams message snippets and associated message metadata, including messages carrying URLs and federated messages. Access is permission controlled: a user needs the Advanced Hunting and message preview permissions, and without them the table is not visible.
items.why: A hunting table that returns message content is a new class of data in the same query surface analysts already hold. The permission gate is the control, and it is the existing message preview permission — so whoever holds that today gains read access to Teams message text through KQL on the day the table lands.
items.action: Before late September, review who holds the Advanced Hunting and message preview permissions, decide whether that set is the set you want reading Teams message content, and record the decision in your investigation procedures.

Listing and retrieving Dataverse organizations through them breaks; environment performance and availability are not affected, and Dataverse Developer Tools such as the CRM SDK and connectors are excluded from the change.
items.why: Three days of notice on an endpoint that inventory and automation scripts call to enumerate Dataverse organizations. Anything that discovers environments before acting on them is the code that breaks first.
items.action: Search your automation for globaldisco.crm.dynamics.com before 21 September and move those calls to the supported discovery route.

items.officialTitle: Retirement of Microsoft 365 Companion apps
items.fingerprint: The Calendar, People and Files companion apps retire on 16 December 2026. From the date of the post Microsoft is phasing out their automatic installation and no longer shipping updates or fixes, security fixes included, while existing installations keep working until the end date. Admins are told to stop new deployments and remove existing installations; no Microsoft 365 data is affected.
