items.action: Inventory the three companion apps across managed devices now, block new installation through your deployment channel, and schedule removal rather than waiting for 16 December.

items.title: A SpaceXAI subprocessor setting appears in the admin center, off by default, unlocking Grok models in Office apps
items.officialTitle: Microsoft Copilot: SpaceXAI subprocessor admin setting
items.fingerprint: SpaceXAI joins Microsoft's Online Services Subprocessor List and a SpaceXAI setting appears under AI providers operating as Microsoft subprocessors in the Microsoft 365 admin center from 18 September 2026. It is disabled by default and only eligible Frontier customers see it; tenants in the EU, EFTA and the UK and all government clouds are excluded from the initial rollout. Enabled, it makes Grok models selectable in Word, Excel and PowerPoint, scoped to users or groups, under Microsoft's Product Terms and DPA. Microsoft states SOC 1 Type II, PCI, FedRAMP and HITRUST certifications are not currently available for SpaceXAI.
items.why: A third-party model provider becomes reachable from inside Office documents on an admin toggle. The default is off and no data is processed until someone turns it on, so the control is real — but the certification gap Microsoft names is the thing a compliance team has to rule on before anybody does.
items.action: Decide the answer before someone asks: review the subprocessor documentation and SpaceXAI's certification position, and record whether the setting stays off. If it goes on, scope it to a group rather than the tenant.

items.title: Planner adds a Capacity view for Plan 3 users with no admin control to turn it off
items.officialTitle: Microsoft Planner: Capacity view
items.fingerprint: Capacity view appears alongside Board, Grid and Schedule on existing plans from early October 2026, completing late October. It is built entirely from existing Planner task data and creates none of its own, needs a Planner Plan 3 licence, is absent from mobile, and Microsoft states it is on by default for eligible users with no admin control to disable it.
items.why: No new data and no new permission, but no off switch either: assignee and date fields already in Planner become a staffing timeline visible to anyone with access to the plan.
items.action: No admin action is available. Tell plan owners the view is coming so nobody is surprised by a workload timeline they did not publish.

items.officialTitleNote: Microsoft publishes no headline for the document as a whole; this is the document identification and revision number the CVRF itself prints.
items.title: Seven CVSS 10.0 elevation-of-privilege CVEs in Microsoft-run cloud services were added to the September release on 17 September
items.officialTitle: Security Update Guide — September 2026 (CVRF revision 716)
items.reference: no MC/RM post — MSRC CVRF only
items.fingerprint: The September 2026 CVRF document, revision 716 with a current release date of 2026-09-18T01:01:29, carries 1,732 CVEs of which 155 are Critical. 495 of them were first published on 13 September or later, and seven of those carry a CVSS base score of 10.0, every one an elevation of privilege in a Microsoft-operated cloud service and every one first published on 17 September: CVE-2026-85889 (Azure AI Foundry), CVE-2026-83944 and CVE-2026-70200 (Azure Logic Apps), CVE-2026-69865 (Microsoft Container Registry), CVE-2026-69843 (Microsoft Fabric), CVE-2026-69399 (Azure Arc) and CVE-2026-62874 (Azure Billing). All seven are flagged Publicly Disclosed:No and Exploited:No with an official remediation level. The two Exploited:Yes CVEs in the document remain CVE-2026-81963 and CVE-2026-85880, both first published 8 September and both already on this page.
items.why: Microsoft fixed these in its own services, so there is no package for a tenant to install and no patch window to book. What there is, is a week in which seven service-side privilege boundaries in Azure were at the top of the scale — the kind of thing an auditor asks about afterwards and a brief is supposed to have recorded on the day.
items.action: Nothing to deploy. Read the seven advisories in the Update Guide, confirm which of those services you actually run, and keep the CVE numbers where your evidence for September lives.

items.officialTitleNote: Microsoft publishes no prose announcement for this file; the title is the commit subject in its own repository.
items.tier0Note: UserAuthMethodWB-WHfB.Create is a create path on a Windows Hello for Business authentication method, which is a credential-issuance surface rather than a read of one.
items.title: Microsoft's Graph deployment map gained five hidden permissions today, four for Teams call events and one that creates a Windows Hello authentication method
items.officialTitle: Weekly Permissions sync 2026-09-18 (#1633)
items.reference: no MC/RM post — deployment map only
items.fingerprint: permissions/new/provisioningInfo.json moved from 1,937 to 1,942 names in commit 82a6561 at 14:00 UTC, adding ChannelCallEvents.Read, ChannelCallEvents.Read.All, ChatCallEvents.Read, ChatCallEvents.Read.All and UserAuthMethodWB-WHfB.Create and removing none. All five carry isHidden true, isEnabled true and environment public. None of the five is in Merill's service-principal dump at HEAD 80698c1 of 17 September, so none can be granted in a readable tenant today. In the same commit permissions.json kept all 927 names and changed one field on 175 of them.
items.why: A permission that is hidden and enabled in the public ring is a consent surface Microsoft is staging, not one it is announcing. The four call-event scopes read Teams channel and chat call events; the fifth creates an authentication method, which is the half of the identity surface where a write is the whole story.
items.action: Nothing to grant and nothing to block while these stay out of the service principal. They are tracked so the day they appear in the tenant is a dated row rather than a discovery.

items.title: Legacy Teams retention policies stop implicitly covering Copilot interactions
items.officialTitle: Microsoft Purview: Data Lifecycle Management-Legacy Teams retention policies covering Copilot will be treated as Teams-only
items.fingerprint: Retention policies scoped to Microsoft Teams that currently also reach Microsoft 365 Copilot interactions will be converted to, and treated as, Teams-only policies; they stop implicitly governing Copilot workloads. Microsoft lists the change as in development for general availability and names no date.
items.why: A retention policy that silently covered Copilot prompts and responses will stop covering them, and nothing in the policy blade changes to say so. A tenant relying on the implicit coverage for eDiscovery or regulatory retention loses that coverage on a date Microsoft has not yet published.
items.action: List retention policies scoped to Teams, check which were relied on for Copilot interaction retention, and create explicit Copilot-scoped policies before the conversion lands.

items.title: Express face enrollment builds a Teams face profile from the meeting camera after opt-in
items.officialTitle: Microsoft Teams: Express face enrollment
items.fingerprint: Users opting in can create a Teams face profile using their camera during eligible meetings. Once enrolled they can be recognised in supported Teams Rooms experiences, which Microsoft says helps identify who is in the room and feeds downstream experiences such as Copilot and recap. Administrators can enable or disable the feature for the organisation.
items.why: This is biometric enrolment through a meeting client rather than a managed enrolment flow, and the resulting template drives identification in rooms. Wherever biometric data carries its own legal basis and retention rules, the tenant-level switch is the control that has to be decided before users are offered the opt-in, not after.
items.action: Decide the organisational position on face profiles before the tenant switch defaults on, record the lawful basis where one is required, and set the Teams admin control explicitly rather than leaving it at the Microsoft default.

items.title: Edge autolaunch on Windows startup becomes an opt-in a policy can pin three ways
items.officialTitle: Microsoft Edge: Autolaunch opt-in experience for managed devices
items.fingerprint: Microsoft Edge gains an opt-in experience letting users on managed devices choose whether Edge launches automatically when Windows starts. Administrators can manage the behaviour with the LaunchEdgeOnWindowsStartupEnabled policy, which takes opt-in, opt-out and user-choice configurations.
items.why: A browser that starts with the session changes what a stolen or unlocked device exposes, and the user-choice setting hands that decision to the user unless the policy is pinned. It is a one-line policy decision that is easier to make before the experience ships than after users have opted themselves in.
items.action: Set LaunchEdgeOnWindowsStartupEnabled explicitly in the Edge management service rather than leaving it at user choice, and note the setting in the managed-device baseline.

items.title: Current Channel build for Microsoft 365 Apps ships the September security fixes; tenants that manage updates themselves have to pull it
items.officialTitle: Updates available for Microsoft 365 Apps for Current Channel
items.fingerprint: Microsoft released a Current Channel update for Microsoft 365 Apps, rolling out gradually from 18 September 2026 PST. Clients that update from the Office CDN need no action; tenants that manage updates themselves have to download and deploy it, and the security fixes in it are the September ones.
items.why: The build carries the month's Office security fixes. A tenant that pins its own update rings does not get them until it deploys this build, so the gap between the Patch Tuesday announcement and the managed-update ring is the exposure window.
items.action: If you manage Microsoft 365 Apps updates yourself rather than from the Office CDN, pull the Current Channel build and schedule it; if you update from the CDN, confirm the ring is not pinned to an older build.
items.deadlineNote: No deadline stated by Microsoft.
items.publishedSource: Published date printed on the Message Center archive page for MC1474415, read 20 September 2026.

items.title: Eight Graph permissions became grantable in the service principal: app certificate trust configuration, cross-tenant content migration and workbooks
items.officialTitleNote: Microsoft publishes no announcement for this; the change is visible only as a diff of the Microsoft Graph service principal.
items.reference: no MC/RM post — service principal only
items.tier0Note: AppCertTrustConfiguration.ReadWrite.All writes the tenant's application certificate trust configuration, which governs which certificates an application may authenticate with.
items.fingerprint: Between the 17 September and the 22 September dumps of the Microsoft Graph service principal, application roles went from 741 to 747 and delegated scopes from 825 to 827, with nothing removed. The six new application roles are AppCertTrustConfiguration.Read.All, AppCertTrustConfiguration.ReadWrite.All, CrossTenantContentMigration.Read.All, CrossTenantContentMigration.ReadWrite.All, Workbooks.Read.All and Workbooks.ReadWrite.All; the two new delegated scopes are Workbooks.Read.All and Workbooks.ReadWrite.All. All eight are enabled. AppCertTrustConfiguration had existed as a delegated scope since 9 May 2026 but reaches application scope only now.
items.why: Two of the eight are a consent surface worth naming. AppCertTrustConfiguration.ReadWrite.All is application-scoped write access to the tenant's app certificate trust configuration — the setting that decides which certificates an application may present to authenticate — so an app holding it can widen what counts as a trusted credential. CrossTenantContentMigration.ReadWrite.All is an application-scoped write over content moving between tenants, which is a bulk data path rather than a single-object one.
items.action: Nothing is granted by this change. Add all six application roles to the consent-review list now, before the first grant request arrives, and decide in advance which of them may ever be consented and by whom. Workbooks.* is the least alarming of the three families; the two AppCertTrustConfiguration roles are the ones to treat as privileged.

items.title: NetworkAccess.Read.All and NetworkAccess.ReadWrite.All silently reach a new Global Secure Access secure-enterprise-browser endpoint
items.officialTitleNote: Microsoft publishes the reach change only in its own permissions data file; there is no release note.
items.reference: no MC/RM post — permissions data file only
items.tier0Note: NetworkAccess.ReadWrite.All now writes the Global Secure Access secure enterprise browser configuration, which is an enforcement control.
items.fingerprint: In the Weekly Permissions sync of 22 September 2026 (commit c1d06c5) NetworkAccess.Read.All gained GET /networkAccess/secureEnterpriseBrowserConfig and NetworkAccess.ReadWrite.All gained both GET and PATCH on the same path. No permission name was added or removed in that file, which stayed at 927 names, and no other scheme or privilege level moved.
items.why: This is the case with no consent prompt. Any application already holding NetworkAccess.ReadWrite.All — granted for network configuration reading — can now PATCH the secure enterprise browser configuration without anyone re-consenting or being asked. The reach of an existing grant widened; the grant did not.
items.action: List the applications holding NetworkAccess.ReadWrite.All in this tenant and confirm each one is still one you would grant that permission to today, knowing it now writes secure enterprise browser configuration. Add PATCH /networkAccess/secureEnterpriseBrowserConfig to what you watch in Graph activity logs.

items.title: Six directory and group permissions gained a dynamic membership processing status endpoint
items.officialTitleNote: Microsoft publishes the reach change only in its own permissions data file; there is no release note.
items.reference: no MC/RM post — permissions data file only
items.fingerprint: The same 22 September sync added GET /groups/dynamicMembershipProcessingStatus(state={value},dynamicMembershipPriority={value}) to Directory.Read.All, Directory.ReadWrite.All, Group.Read.All, Group.ReadWrite.All, GroupMember.Read.All and GroupMember.ReadWrite.All. Nothing was removed from any of the six.
items.why: A read-only status endpoint is a small thing on its own, but it is reachable by GroupMember.ReadWrite.All, whose endpoint list was five paths and is now six — a permission that narrow is worth knowing the exact shape of.
items.action: No action. Recorded so the endpoint count on those six permissions is a dated row rather than a surprise the next time someone audits them.

items.title: Web based enrollment becomes the default for iOS and iPadOS, and it needs the SSO extension and just-in-time registration to work
items.officialTitle: Plan for Change: Web based device enrollment will become default method for iOS/iPadOS device enrollment
items.deadlineNote: Microsoft states only "Starting in early 2027" and prints no day, so no date is asserted here.
items.fingerprint: From early 2027 the preselected enrollment type when creating an iOS or iPadOS enrollment profile changes from Device enrollment with Company Portal to Web based device enrollment, and new tenants with no enrollment profile get the web flow by default. Existing profiles are not changed. Web enrollment requires the single sign-on extension policy so that just-in-time registration can run; without it and Microsoft Authenticator, users may be unable to complete device registration. Requires iOS/iPadOS 15 or later.
items.why: Just-in-time registration is what creates the Entra device record. If the SSO extension policy is not deployed when the default flips, devices enrol into Intune but never register in Entra, so device-based Conditional Access and compliance gates have nothing to evaluate and users are blocked from protected resources.
items.action: Deploy the SSO extension policy to iOS and iPadOS now, verify Microsoft Authenticator is available on those devices, and confirm the enrollment type on every existing iOS profile at Devices > Enrollment > Apple > Enrollment Options > Enrollment types so the flip changes nothing you did not choose.

items.title: A Microsoft-managed "Agent 365 CLI" enterprise application appears in Entra without an admin creating it
items.officialTitle: Microsoft Agent 365: Simplified Agent 365 CLI setup experience
items.tier0Note: A first-party service principal appears in the tenant directory without an administrator creating it.
items.fingerprint: A Microsoft-managed enterprise application named Agent 365 CLI now appears in Microsoft Entra for eligible tenants, removing the need for an admin to register and maintain a tenant-owned client application for Agent 365 CLI setup. Generally available worldwide now. Existing customer-owned app registrations keep working and need no change. Conditional Access and Security Defaults still apply and the CLI uses delegated access under the signed-in user.
items.why: A new service principal that nobody in the tenant created is exactly the thing an app-registration alert fires on, and it will be read as suspicious by any team that watches for it. It is also a delegated-access path, so Conditional Access — including any device-code restriction — governs it.
items.action: Tell whoever triages new enterprise applications that Agent 365 CLI is expected, so it is not chased as a rogue registration. If device-code authentication is restricted, re-check that restriction against the CLI, which Microsoft calls out specifically for WSL, macOS and Linux.

items.title: Agent Registry merges duplicate agent entries, so agent counts drop without any agent going away
items.officialTitle: Microsoft 365 admin center: Agent Registry consolidates duplicate agent entries and adds version history
items.fingerprint: The Agent Registry consolidates duplicate agent entries into single records carrying accessible version history; the most recent organizational version shows by default with a version selector in agent details. Rolling out from mid-September 2026 to late September 2026. Microsoft states no action is required.
items.why: No action is required and the number still moves. Anyone using Agent Registry totals as an AI-inventory control metric will see the count fall during the rollout and has to decide whether that is consolidation or agents disappearing — which is a question the registry itself cannot answer after the fact.
items.action: Record today's agent count before the rollout reaches the tenant, so the drop can be reconciled rather than investigated.

items.title: Remediation actions move into the Teams message entity flyout, closing the Teams triage-to-containment loop
items.officialTitle: Microsoft Defender for Office 365: Remediation actions from the Teams message entity flyout
items.fingerprint: Analysts can trigger remediation actions directly from the Teams message entity flyout in Microsoft Defender for Office 365, rather than leaving the entity view for a separate remediation workflow. Rollout spans September and October 2026.
items.why: It pairs with the MessageContents advanced hunting table landing in the same weeks: the content is queryable in one place and the action is now available in the same pane, so the Teams phishing path is investigate-and-respond inside one portal.
items.action: Update the Teams phishing playbook to take the flyout action, and re-check who holds the remediation permission now that the action sits one click from triage.

items.title: Integrated Security Operations Center reaches preview for Defender customers who have no Sentinel workspace
items.officialTitle: Integrated Security Operations Center (ISOC) in Microsoft Defender
items.fingerprint: Microsoft states that starting 23 September 2026 the Integrated Security Operations Center is available to eligible Microsoft Defender Suite, Microsoft 365 E5 and E7 customers that do not have an active Microsoft Sentinel workspace, with 30 days of included retention for Defender data during the preview. Case management, Workbooks, natural-language playbook generation and enhanced automation rules need no ISOC workspace; UEBA, Content hub, CI/CD repositories, threat intelligence and Azure or third-party ingestion require one. Microsoft warns explicitly not to disconnect a production Sentinel workspace in order to qualify.
items.why: It is the first day of a preview that changes what a Defender-only tenant can do without buying Sentinel, and the eligibility rule — no active Sentinel workspace — is the kind of condition that invites someone to disconnect a production workspace to qualify. Microsoft says in as many words not to.
items.action: If the tenant has no Sentinel workspace, read the eligibility and retention terms before enabling, because the 30-day included retention is a preview term rather than a plan. If it does have one, do nothing: the correct answer is to leave it connected.

items.title: Cloud Sync provisioning agent 1.1.2505.0 drops the Domain Admin requirement with a gMSA and removes Repair-AADCloudSyncToolsAccount
items.officialTitle: Microsoft Entra provisioning Agent: Version release history
items.tier0Note: The provisioning agent's service account is a hybrid identity write path into on-premises Active Directory.
items.fingerprint: Release date 21 September 2026, corrected from 16 September on 17 September. The release carries a security hardening section, and the agent no longer requires Domain Admin credentials when a gMSA with custom gMSA permissions is supplied. Repair-AADCloudSyncToolsAccount has been removed from the AADCloudSyncTools PowerShell module. Fixes cover unresolved cross-domain directory references causing object-level quarantine in AD2AADProvisioning jobs and domain controller affinity paging with nested OUs.
items.why: Dropping the Domain Admin requirement is a real reduction in standing privilege on the hybrid sync path, and it is available the moment the agent is upgraded. The removed cmdlet is the other half: any runbook that calls Repair-AADCloudSyncToolsAccount breaks on upgrade rather than warning.
items.action: Grep the automation estate for Repair-AADCloudSyncToolsAccount before upgrading. Then upgrade, and take the chance to move the agent onto a gMSA with custom permissions so the Domain Admin grant can be withdrawn.

items.title: Global Secure Access allows up to ten custom Private Access forwarding profiles, and priority decides which one applies
items.officialTitle: Global Secure Access traffic forwarding profiles
items.tier0Note: A forwarding profile decides which users reach which private applications, so its priority is an access control.
items.fingerprint: Tenants can create custom Private Access traffic forwarding profiles in addition to the single default one, up to ten during preview. Each custom profile carries its own acquisition rules, assignments, status and priority, and profiles can be assigned to users, groups, devices and device platforms, with nested group membership supported. When several enabled profiles for the same traffic type apply to a user and device, only the applicable profile with the highest priority is used. Deleted custom profiles cannot be restored.
items.why: Priority is now the thing that decides who reaches which private application, and priority is a field rather than an assignment. A change to it re-scopes access without any assignment changing, which is invisible to a review that reads assignments only.
items.action: Add create, modify and delete of traffic forwarding profiles to Global Secure Access audit log monitoring, and treat a priority change as an access change in review. The stated use case — excluding privileged applications from a broadly assigned profile — is worth building deliberately rather than inheriting.

items.title: Microsoft corrects what PIM for Groups actually protects: eligible members and owners were always in scope, and non-role-assignable groups never were
items.officialTitle: Privileged Identity Management for Groups
items.publishedNote: The page still prints ms.date 23 April 2026; the correction reached the public entra-docs live branch on 22 September 2026 and Microsoft did not bump the printed date.
items.tier0Note: The corrected sentence describes who can reset the credentials of a user who can elevate to an Entra role.
items.fingerprint: Microsoft replaced the statement that for role-assignable groups no other users can change the credentials of the users who are active members, with: credential protection covers the members and owners of the group, including eligible members and owners who have not activated yet. The accompanying note adds that groups used for role elevation must be created as role-assignable, and that changing the credentials of members and owners of a role-assignable group requires at least the Privileged Authentication Administrator role.
items.why: The old sentence understated the protection in one direction and overstated it in another. The practical consequence is the second half: a group that grants an Entra role but was not created role-assignable gives its eligible members no credential protection at all, so a Helpdesk, Authentication or User Administrator can reset their password and then elevate. That is a documented escalation path, and it is a configuration mistake rather than a vulnerability.
items.action: List every group that grants an Entra role and check isAssignableToRole on each. Any that is false is the finding; it cannot be changed after creation, so the group has to be recreated as role-assignable and the assignments moved.

items.title: Azure Blueprints stops accepting new assignments on 31 October, and its resource locks stop working at full retirement
items.officialTitle: Azure Blueprints retirement
items.publishedNote: Microsoft prints no publication date on the retirement page; the timeline has been extended more than once since the original 2023 announcement.
items.deadlineNote: 31 Oct 2026 ends modification of blueprint definitions and creation of new assignments; 31 Dec 2026 ends modification of existing assignments; 31 Jan 2027 is full retirement, when the API stops responding and unexported content is permanently deleted.
items.fingerprint: Phased retirement. From 31 October 2026 existing blueprint definitions can no longer be modified and new blueprint assignments can no longer be created. From 31 December 2026 existing assignments can no longer be modified. On 31 January 2027 the API stops responding, the CLI and PowerShell commands stop, Blueprints is removed from the portal, and unexported definitions, versions and assignments are permanently deleted.
items.why: Blueprint assignments can apply Do Not Delete and Read Only locks. Those locks stop functioning at retirement, so any resource whose protection rests on a blueprint lock silently loses it — and the definitions that describe what was being protected are deleted at the same time.
items.action: Export every blueprint definition, version and assignment you intend to keep before 31 January 2027, and before 31 October decide the replacement for each lock: Azure Policy deny or denyAction for the rule, and a resource lock for the deletion protection.

items.title: Microsoft-provided SMS and voice retirement splits into two waves: Global Administrators and external users move to 1 July 2027
items.officialTitle: (Updated) Microsoft Entra: Passkeys by default and retirement of Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication
items.deadlineNote: 1 Feb 2027 for most users; 1 Jul 2027 for Global Administrators and external users. Internal guest users are not in the July group and keep the February date.
items.tier0Note: The retirement removes an MFA method that privileged accounts may still be registered for.
items.fingerprint: Updated 15 September 2026: Microsoft added a second retirement wave. Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication retires on 1 February 2027 for most users and on 1 July 2027 for Global Administrators and external users. Internal guest users are not included in the July group and still follow the 1 February 2027 date. The temporary tenant opt-out covers only 1 September 2026 to 1 February 2027 and there is no opt-out from enforcement.
items.why: The later date applies to the accounts you would least want to lock out and most want off SMS: Global Administrators. Splitting the population means an inventory taken before 15 September no longer matches the deadlines, and the internal-guest carve-out is narrow enough to be read the wrong way.
items.action: Re-cut the SMS and voice inventory into three populations — Global Administrators, external users, everyone else including internal guests — and give each its own date. Move the administrators first: they are last in Microsoft's order and should be first in yours.

items.title: Passkey as a first MFA method is pulled forward to early October, so registration can happen from a session that never proved anything
items.officialTitle: Microsoft Entra: Users can register a passkey or passwordless sign-in as their first multifactor authentication method
items.deadlineNote: Microsoft states phase 1 general availability worldwide and GCC from early October 2026 to mid-November 2026, and phase 2 to late February 2027; no action-by date is given.
items.tier0Note: First-method credential registration is an account-takeover persistence path when the registering session is unverified.
items.fingerprint: Updated 14 September 2026, pulling phase 1 forward from mid-October to early October 2026. Password-only users will be able to register a passkey as their first multifactor method, removing the prior requirement to register SMS or voice first. Phase 1 covers synced passkeys, Microsoft Entra passkeys on Windows and FIDO2 security keys; phase 2 adds Windows Hello for Business, macOS Platform SSO, the Authenticator app passkey and Authenticator passwordless sign-in. Microsoft recommends reviewing Conditional Access policies related to security information registration and considering requiring MFA to register security information.
items.why: A user with only a password can now register a phishing-resistant credential in one step. That is the point of the feature and it is also the risk: if the registration session itself is not gated, an attacker holding a stolen password registers a passkey and has durable, phishing-resistant persistence that survives a password reset.
items.action: Before early October, put a Conditional Access policy on the security information registration action requiring MFA or a trusted location, and add first-time passkey registration from an unfamiliar device or country to the hunting queue.

items.title: Microsoft starts onboarding Sentinel tenants to the Defender portal automatically and picks the primary workspace itself
items.officialTitle: Automatic onboarding for Microsoft Sentinel
items.reference: no MC/RM post — Partner Center announcement
items.deadlineNote: 31 Mar 2027 is the stated retirement of the Microsoft Sentinel experience in the Azure portal.
items.fingerprint: Microsoft begins automatically onboarding managed customers that have not moved to the unified Microsoft Sentinel experience in the Defender portal. Microsoft selects one primary workspace for Microsoft Defender XDR alerts and incidents; XDR-dependent content in secondary workspaces might stop functioning once the primary workspace is established. Tenant administrators receive an in-portal banner and an administrator email about 30 days ahead. A different primary workspace can be requested by email to MSSP-Sentinel-Support@microsoft.com with the tenant ID and preferred workspace resource ID.
items.why: Microsoft chooses the primary workspace, and the choice decides which analytics rules, automation rules, playbooks and workbooks keep working. In a multi-workspace tenant the wrong choice silently breaks detection content that is not in the chosen workspace.
items.action: Inventory tenants with more than one Sentinel workspace now and decide which one should be primary, so the 30-day notice is a confirmation rather than a discovery. Where the answer is not Microsoft's default, send the request before the banner appears.

items.title: App Gallery onboarding becomes self-service for publishers, so new consent targets will appear faster
items.officialTitle: Public preview of self-service onboarding for new Microsoft Entra App Gallery applications
items.fingerprint: Independent software vendors can now submit App Gallery applications themselves, validating single sign-on and provisioning, resolving issues earlier and managing submissions end to end, rather than going through a Microsoft-driven onboarding process.
items.why: The effect on a tenant is indirect but real: a faster onboarding pipeline means more gallery applications, and every gallery application is a potential consent and provisioning target that a user can reach.
items.action: No action today. Take it as a reason to confirm that user consent is restricted to a vetted set and that new enterprise application creation is alerted on.

items.title: Purview DLP extends to Microsoft Cowork, applying existing Copilot policies to a second AI surface automatically
items.officialTitle: Microsoft Purview: Data Loss Prevention for Microsoft Cowork
items.deadlineNote: Microsoft states rollout begins late September 2026 and gives no action-by date.
items.fingerprint: Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention expands to cover Microsoft Cowork, applying existing and new Microsoft Copilot DLP policies automatically. The named capabilities are grounding DLP based on sensitivity labels, which prevents Copilot and Cowork from processing knowledge sources carrying specified labels; prompt DLP based on sensitive information types; and web search DLP. Roadmap ID 570845. Rollout begins late September 2026 with no required user action.
items.why: Existing Copilot DLP policies start applying to a surface they were not written for, automatically and with no user action. That is the right default, and it also means the first time anyone finds out which of their policies bite in Cowork is when a user is blocked.
items.action: Before late September, re-read the Copilot DLP policies as if they governed Cowork — because from the rollout they do — and check the grounding rules in particular, since a Highly Confidential label that merely narrowed Copilot answers now narrows a second product.

items.title: Auto-labeling will apply a SharePoint library's default sensitivity label to files that already exist in it
items.officialTitle: Microsoft Purview | Information Protection: Apply default SharePoint library sensitivity labels to data at rest
items.deadlineNote: Microsoft states general availability worldwide beginning early October 2026 and gives no action-by date.
items.fingerprint: A new auto-labeling policy applies a SharePoint document library's default sensitivity label to files that already exist in that library, where previously default library labels reached only new or modified files. It is opt-in, requires administrator configuration, and supports up to ten SharePoint sites per policy. Roadmap ID 559105. General availability worldwide begins early October 2026.
items.why: Applying a label to historical content changes what encryption and access restrictions apply to files nobody has touched in years. It is opt-in, which is the control; the risk is enabling it on a site whose default label carries protection that the existing content's readers do not have rights to.
items.action: Before enabling it on any site, confirm what the default library label actually enforces and who would lose access. Start with one site rather than the ten the policy allows.

graphMap.rule: resource = first path segment that is not a parameter; /me/... counts as users. Directory action microsoft.directory/<resource>[/<property>]/<operation>; a .unified or .security suffix on the resource falls back to its base. GET maps to read, POST to create, PATCH and PUT to update, DELETE to delete. A role covers an endpoint when it holds an action on the same resource with the same operation, or allTasks on that resource. Coverage is the share of the permission's ENDPOINTS, never the count of the role's actions. Depth is whole resource when the matching action carries allProperties or allTasks, and selected properties only otherwise.
graphMap.ruleNote: Derived by this brief, not published by Microsoft. Microsoft publishes no role-to-permission mapping: permissions.json carries authorizationType, ownerInfo, pathSets and schemes and no role field at all, and the 136 role source files in MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs name no Graph permission.

items.text: This release includes security fixes. We recommend upgrading to this version as soon as possible.

Added a guided migration workflow from Microsoft Entra Connect Sync to Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync. The workflow includes configuration assessment, provisioning agent setup, staged activation, and validation. This feature is available only in the Azure public cloud.
Added support for an additional sovereign cloud environment, including Pass-through Authentication, Seamless Single Sign-On, password writeback, and Health Agent monitoring.

Phishing-resistant authentication in the Microsoft Entra Connect setup wizard is now generally available and enabled by default. The Windows Web Account Manager prompt supports passkeys, FIDO2 security keys, and passwords, reuses the signed-in session across Microsoft Entra services, and preserves Seamless Single Sign-On Kerberos key rotation.

Cloud configuration cmdlets no longer require an explicit -AADUserName. When you omit the parameter, Microsoft Entra Connect derives a sign-in hint from the connector configuration and opens an interactive sign-in prompt. This behavior applies to Set-ADSyncAADCompanyFeature, Set-ADSyncAADPasswordSyncState, Enable-ADSyncExportDeletionThreshold, Set-ADSyncScheduler, and Set-ADSyncDirSyncConfiguration.

The Select Containers dialog in Synchronization Service Manager is now read-only. You can still use the dialog to view the current selections. To make changes, use Customize synchronization options in the Microsoft Entra Connect wizard.
When you configure Seamless Single Sign-On by using the standalone PowerShell module, you must import ADSync.psd1 before AzureADSSO.psd1.
Updated the bundled SQL Server 2022 LocalDB from version 16.0.4250.1 to 16.0.4262.2.
Fixed an Application-Based Authentication certificate rotation issue that could remove the last usable application key during directory replica delays.

Fixed an issue where expanding a previously deselected domain on the Domain and OU filtering page could reselect the domain and enable synchronization for the entire domain after the wizard completed.
Fixed multiple security vulnerabilities in bundled third-party dependencies and hardened local temporary-file permissions and SharePoint connector profile-image downloads.

Microsoft Graph permissions have been added to Microsoft Entra Connect. If you use app-scoped Conditional Access policies, review policies targeting Microsoft.Azure.SyncFabric or Microsoft 365 Reporting Service.
Fixed an issue where installing or upgrading Microsoft Entra Connect with an existing ADSync database could fail with error 0xE0474352.
Fixed an issue where upgrading Microsoft Entra Connect didn't update an installed Microsoft Visual C++ 2015-2022 Redistributable version earlier than 14.41.
Fixed an issue where the Microsoft Entra Connect wizard could close during startup when the Windows PowerShell Transcription policy contained an invalid output directory.
Fixed an issue where Synchronization Service Manager could close unexpectedly when you opened Connector Properties and listed directory partitions.
Fixed an issue where Change Credentials didn't open for connector rows outside the visible area on configurations with many Active Directory connectors.

add: # Assign users and devices to traffic forwarding profiles

You can assign specific users, groups, devices, and device platforms to a Global Secure Access traffic forwarding profile. Assignments let you deploy a profile gradually and provide different traffic acquisition rules to different users and devices.
This article explains assignments for traffic forwarding profiles, including custom Private Access profiles.
To manage assignments, you must have:

- A [Global Secure Access Administrator](../identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference.md#global-secure-access-administrator) role in Microsoft Entra ID to view and manage the traffic forwarding profile.
- The required Global Secure Access product licenses. For details, see [What is Global Secure Access](overview-what-is-global-secure-access.md).
rem: # How to assign users and groups to traffic forwarding profiles

With the Global Secure Access traffic forwarding features, you can assign specific users and groups to a traffic forwarding profile. User or group assignment limits the scope of the traffic forwarding profile so you have a mechanism to roll out the profile safely and at a controlled pace.
This article describes how to assign specific users and groups to a traffic forwarding profile.
To assign a traffic forwarding profile to specific users and groups, you must have:

- A [Global Secure Access Administrator](../identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference.md#global-secure-access-administrator) role in Microsoft Entra ID to view the traffic forwarding profile.
- An [Application Administrator](../identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference.md#application-administrator) role to assign the traffic profile to the selected users and groups.

Account discovery retrieves users and groups from a target application and classifies them into three categories:

- **Local identities** — Users or groups in the target application that have no corresponding user or group in Microsoft Entra ID. These identities might belong to former employees, service accounts, users who were provisioned through a different process, groups created directly in the target applic

- **Unassigned identities** — Users or groups that match a user or group in Microsoft Entra ID but aren't assigned to the enterprise application. These identities exist in your directory but don't have the required application assignment for provisioning to manage them.

- **Assigned identities** — Users or groups that match a user or group in Microsoft Entra ID and are assigned to the enterprise application. These identities are fully managed by the provisioning service.

pages.name: Azure Container Apps — Manage secrets
pages.socNote: Names the six built-in roles whose wildcard actions include listSecrets, which returns secret values in plain text. Carried from the 20 September read; this page did not move again in the three days since.

add: ## Permissions for managing secrets

Azure Container Apps exposes separate `listSecrets` operations for container apps, jobs, and Dapr components. These operations return secret values in plain text. Grant these permissions only to identities that need to read secret values.

Several Azure built-in roles for Container Apps define permissions using wildcard patterns as a convenience. The following examples grant the ability to read secret values through a wildcard or explicit `listSecrets` permission, even when the role name or description suggests narrower access. This list isn't exhaustive; review the current [Azure built-in roles for containers](/azure/role-based-access-control/built-in-roles/containers) before assigning a role.
The following roles grant access to container app or job secret values:
| Built-in role | Relevant permissions in the role definition | Matching secrets operation |
| Container Apps Contributor | `Microsoft.App/containerApps/*/action` | `Microsoft.App/containerApps/listSecrets/action` |
| Container Apps Operator | `Microsoft.App/containerApps/*/action` | `Microsoft.App/containerApps/listSecrets/action` |
| Container Apps Jobs Contributor | `Microsoft.App/jobs/*/action` | `Microsoft.App/jobs/listSecrets/action` |
| Container Apps Jobs Operator | `Microsoft.App/jobs/*/action` | `Microsoft.App/jobs/listSecrets/action` |

pages.name: Microsoft Entra ID Protection — How to export risk data
pages.socNote: Names the Log Analytics table behind each ID Protection diagnostic setting category, including the two agent-identity tables. A hunting query written against the category name returns nothing and raises no error. Carried from the 20 September read; this page did not move again in the three days since.

add: The names you select in **diagnostic settings** are not the same as the **table names** you use in Kusto (KQL) queries.
### Diagnostic setting categories vs Log Analytics table names
| Report / signal | Diagnostic setting category (enable export) | Log Analytics table name (use in queries) |
| Risky users | `RiskyUsers` | `AADRiskyUsers` |
| Risk detections (users) | `UserRiskEvents` | `AADUserRiskEvents` |
| Risky workload identities | `RiskyServicePrincipals` | `AADRiskyServicePrincipals` |
| Workload identity detections | `ServicePrincipalRiskEvents` | `AADServicePrincipalRiskEvents` |
| Risky agents | `RiskyAgents` | `AADRiskyAgents` |
| Agent identity detections | `AgentRiskEvents` | `AADAgentRiskEvents` |
remove: - RiskyUsers - Provides data like the **Risky users** report.
- UserRiskEvents - Provides data like the **Risk detections** report.
- RiskyServicePrincipals - Provides data like the **Risky workload identities** report.
- ServicePrincipalRiskEvents - Provides data like the **Workload identity detections** report.
- RiskyAgents - Provides data like the **Risky agents** report.
- AgentRiskEvents - Provides data like the **Agent identity detections** report.

add: | DSREG_TOKEN_MISSING_ON_PREM_ID(0x801c0095) | The token doesn't contain an on-premises ID. | The Kerberos ticket from the on-premises Kerberos authority doesn't contain information required by Microsoft Entra ID. | On every domain controller that runs Windows Server 2025 within the Active Directory domain, make sure it runs [build 26100.6905](https://support.microsoft.com/topic/october-23-2025-kb5070881-os-build-26100-6905-out-of-band-8e7ac742-6785-4677-87e4-b73dd8ac0122) or later. |

Make sure the KDC service is running on this domain controller, and this domain controller can be contacted by the computer trying to perform the hybrid join. changes.title: Memory scan for Linux
changes.text: Memory Scan extends Microsoft Defender for Endpoint protection capabilities on Linux by enabling inspection of process memory for known malicious behaviours and memory-resident threats, providing an additional layer of protection against advanced attacks. Memory-resident threats are increasingly challenging for security teams because they can execute directly in memory with little or no footprint on disk, making them more difficult to detect using traditional file-based scanning techniques. Memory Scan helps improve visibility into these threats and strengthens protection against sophisticated attack methods such as in-memory malware and malicious code injection. Available in Defender version 101.26071.0005 or later in Insiders-slow channel.

changes.title: Operating system version property in assignment filters is generally available
changes.text: The operatingSystemVersion property in assignment filters is now generally available for managed devices and managed apps. Use this property to create filter rules that scope your app and policy assignments to devices running a specific OS version or build range. changes.title: New Microsoft Secure Score recommendation
changes.text: Microsoft Secure Score now includes the Reduce unnecessary inbound internet exposure on internet-facing devices recommendation, which helps identify devices that are accessible from the public internet and may represent unnecessary attack surface. Internet-facing devices are primary entry points for attackers and automated scanners, making them prime targets for credential brute-forcing, exploitation of unpatched vulnerabilities, and initial access for ransomware and hands-on-keyboard intrusions. This recommendation provides centralized visibility into internet-facing devices across the environment, enabling organizations to validate whether exposure is expected, prioritize remediation for unintended exposure, and reduce external attack surface at scale.

changes.title: Microsoft Edge > Maximum number of concurrent connections to the proxy server for WebSocket requests
changes.text: Specifies the maximum number of simultaneous connections to a proxy server for WebSocket requests. To configure limits for non-WebSocket requests, see the MaxConnectionsPerProxy policy. If you don't configure this policy, the default value of 32 is used. Some web applications maintain multiple concurrent connections, like long-lived or hanging requests. Setting a value lower than the default may cause networking delays when many such applications are open. Some proxy servers can't handle a high number of concurrent connections per client. In these cases, reducing the value of this policy might improve reliability. The supported range is 6 to 256: - Values less than 6 are treated as 6. - Values greater than 256 are treated as 256. Modify this value only if required by your proxy server configuration or network environment. MaxConnectionsPerProxyForWebSocket

Previously, renewing an issuing CA required creating a new CA and manually updating dependent SCEP certificate profiles, which increased operational overhead and configuration risk. With in-place renewal, certificate issuance continues uninterrupted for scenarios such as Wi-Fi, VPN, and email, without changes to existing SCEP profiles or device assignments. For more information, see Renew a certification authority in Cloud PKI.

changes.title: Strict Tunnel Mode for Microsoft Tunnel on Android
changes.text: Microsoft Tunnel now supports Strict Tunnel Mode on Android Enterprise devices. When Strict Tunnel Mode is enabled, all network traffic is forced through the VPN tunnel. If the VPN connection is unavailable or drops, all network traffic on the device is blocked until the VPN reconnects, preventing apps from accessing the public internet outside of the tunnel. Strict Tunnel Mode is available when a Microsoft Tunnel VPN profile is configured with Always-on VPN. Admins can configure an app exclusion list to allow specific apps to bypass the tunnel and connect directly to the network, regardless of VPN connection status. Strict Tunnel Mode requires devices enrolled through Android Management API (AM API). changes.why: Adds or alters a detection, so alert volume and coverage move with it.

changes.title: After
changes.text: Analytics: user@domain.com -> Automation rule Account Name: user + UPNSuffix : domain.com What you need to do Update any automation rules or logic apps that compare against the full UPN. Replace direct equality checks with separate comparisons for the UPN prefix and UPN suffix. We strongly recommend using Contains and Starts with operations instead of strict equality to maintain compatibility both before and after the change. For example, replace conditions such as AccountName Equals user@domain.com with logic like: - AccountName Contains user or Starts with user - UPNSuffix Equals domain.com / Starts with domain.com / Contains domain.com For more information, including before and after examples, read the blog article Update: Changing the Account Name Entity Mapping in Microsoft Sentinel.

changes.title: General Availability - Synced passkeys in Microsoft Entra ID
changes.text: Type: General Availability Service category: Authentications (Logins) Product capability: User Authentication Microsoft Entra ID now supports synced passkeys as a generally available authentication method. Synced passkeys are FIDO2-based credentials that can be stored in built-in or third-party passkey providers and made available across a user’s devices. changes.title: New Microsoft Secure Score recommendations
changes.text: Microsoft Secure Score now includes new recommendations to help organizations proactively prevent common endpoint attack techniques: - Block outbound network connections from Microsoft HTML Application Host (mshta.exe): Helps mitigate attacks that leverage mshta.exe (a trusted Windows binary) to execute malicious scripts and communicate with external command-and-control (C2) infrastructure. Blocking outbound connections from mshta.exe disrupts common attack chains, prevents payload download and data exfiltration, and reduces the risk of living-off-the-land attacks. This is relevant for emerging attack campaigns, for example, ClickFix campaigns, where attackers abuse legitimate tools like mshta.exe to execute malicious content delivered through user interaction.

changes.title: Connectivity > Disable Cross Device Resume
changes.text: This feature lets Windows suggest continuing an activity users start on a device, like a phone, to a PC. IT admins can use this policy to turn off this feature and prevent users from continuing tasks, like browsing files or continuing to use supported apps that require linking between a phone and PC. When set to CrossDeviceResume is Disabled , the Windows device doesn't receive any CrossDeviceResume notification. Users won't see any "resume from your phone" prompts. When you select CrossDeviceResume is Enabled , the Windows device does receive notification to resume activity from linked devices. If you don't configure this policy setting, the default behavior is that the CrossDeviceResume feature is turned on, which means users see the notification. Changes to this policy take effect on reboot. This policy: - Is available to Windows Insiders. - Uses the DisableCrossDeviceResume CSP.

changes.title: Call to action: update queries and automation by July 1, 2026 - standardized account entity naming in incidents and alerts
changes.text: Microsoft Sentinel is updating how it identifies account entities in incidents and alerts. This change introduces a standardized naming logic to improve consistency and reliability across your analytics and automation workflows. Microsoft Sentinel will now select the most reliable account identifier using the following priority: 1. UPN prefix – the part before “@” in a User Principal Name - Example: john.doe@contoso.com → john.doe 1. Name – used if UPN prefix is unavailable 1. Display Name – fallback if both above are missing Update your KQL queries and automation logic to follow the new precedence-aware pattern. Use the coalesce() (/kusto/query/coalesce-function) function to ensure compatibility: kql

recent.title: Memory scan for Linux
recent.text: Memory Scan extends Microsoft Defender for Endpoint protection capabilities on Linux by enabling inspection of process memory for known malicious behaviours and memory-resident threats, providing an additional layer of protection against advanced attacks. Memory-resident threats are increasingly challenging for security teams because they can execute directly in memory with little or no footprint on disk, making them more difficult to detect using traditional file-based scanning techniques. Memory Scan helps improve visibility into these threats and strengthens protection against sophisticated attack methods such as in-memory malware and malicious code injection. Available in Defender version 101.26071.0005 or later in Insiders-slow channel.

recent.title: Configure screen timeout for corporate Android devices
recent.text: Microsoft Intune now supports a Screen timeout setting in the Android Enterprise settings catalog, letting you specify how many seconds pass before the screen turns off. Configure it under Devices > Manage devices > Configuration > Create > New policy > Android Enterprise > Settings catalog . The value must stay at or below Time to lock screen and applies to fully managed and dedicated devices on Android 9 and later, and corporate-owned work profile devices on Android 15 and later.

recent.title: Separate device and work profile passwords on Android Enterprise devices
recent.text: Microsoft Intune now supports the Block one lock for device and work profile setting in the Android Enterprise settings catalog, letting you require separate locks for the device and work profile instead of a shared one. Set it to True after configuring a work profile password requirement. The default, False , allows a common lock. The setting supports Android 9 and later.

recent.title: Limit how long an Android work profile can stay off
recent.text: Microsoft Intune now supports the Number of days work profile is allowed to be switched off setting in the Android Enterprise settings catalog, so you can limit how long a work profile stays turned off. Enter the maximum number of days, with a minimum of three, or enter 0 to disable the restriction. There's no documented upper limit, giving you flexibility for your organization's needs.

recent.title: Remove eSIMs during a device wipe with a settings catalog policy
recent.text: Microsoft Intune now supports the Remove all eSIMs during a device wipe setting in the Android Enterprise settings catalog. Set it to True to request removal of all eSIMs when a corporate-owned device is wiped while the policy applies. The default, False , doesn't request removal, although the operating system might still remove eSIMs when required. The setting supports Android 15 and later.

recent.text: Microsoft Intune now supports new Settings Catalog options for testing on the OS 27 betas, covering Declarative Device Management areas such as App Settings , Web Content Filter , and Siri Settings for iOS/iPadOS and macOS. Configure them under Devices > Manage devices > Configuration > Create > New policy > iOS/iPadOS or macOS > Settings catalog . This lets you test upcoming Apple management controls ahead of general availability. For more information, see Create a policy using settings catalog.

recent.title: New policy settings for Windows
recent.text: Microsoft Intune now includes new Windows settings catalog options across several administrative template refreshes. Highlights include Turn on Protected Mode controls for Internet Explorer security zones, new Microsoft Edge policies from the Edge 150 template refresh, and a Disconnect if a Remote Desktop Services session when no smart card is present option for interactive logon. The Microsoft Office templates also gained new settings. Create a Windows settings catalog profile to configure them.

recent.title: View expanded SIM inventory for corporate-owned Android devices
recent.text: Microsoft Intune now surfaces expanded SIM inventory for corporate-owned Android Enterprise devices, including EIDs, multiple ICCIDs, and activation state. View these details under Devices > All devices > select a device > Hardware , and use the reported ICCID to identify the correct eSIM for a removal action. EID reporting requires Android 13 and later; full inventory requires Android 15 and later.

recent.title: Activate an eSIM on a corporate-owned Android device
recent.text: Microsoft Intune now supports single-device eSIM activation for corporate-owned Android Enterprise devices running Android 15 and later. Turn on Preview new device view , select the device, then select Activate eSIM and enter the carrier activation code. Intune sends the request without first blocking it based on reported eSIM slot capacity and surfaces errors returned by Google. Personally owned work profile devices aren't supported.

recent.title: Remove an individual eSIM from a corporate-owned Android device
recent.text: Microsoft Intune now lets you remove a single eSIM from a corporate-owned Android Enterprise device without wiping it. Turn on Preview new device view , select the device, copy the eSIM's ICCID from device inventory, then select Remove eSIM and enter the ICCID. The action supports fully managed and dedicated devices on Android 15 and later, and work profile devices on Android 17 and later.

recent.title: Device inventory for personally owned devices on Android Enterprise
recent.text: Microsoft Intune now supports device inventory for personally owned Android Enterprise devices with a work profile managed by Android Management API. View these devices from the device's Inventory page alongside corporate-owned devices in Resource Explorer, and query them with Multi-Device Query. Inventory data is a subset of corporate-owned data; properties such as IMEI, ICCID, and MAC address aren't available. This gives you more consistent analytics across mixed corporate and BYOD environments.

recent.text: Microsoft Sentinel UEBA expands coverage with new data sources for both the behaviors layer and anomaly detection. recent.text: The SAP agentless solution version 1.1.12 adds audit log performance enhancements and the force-sal-filesystem parameter. #customer intent: As a data scientist, I want to fine-tune a premium healthcare model so that I can improve model performance for my domain-specific use case.

add: Fine-tuning adapts a premium healthcare AI model to your institution's data distribution and reporting conventions while the model's fundamental task stays the same. Its output aligns more closely to your label vocabulary and institutional style.

To fine-tune a model, you prepare and upload a model-specific training file, create a fine-tuning job, and deploy the result. A job can remain pending until training capacity is available, moves to running, and then reaches a terminal status.
> [!NOTE]
> Premium healthcare models use the OpenAI Python client's Files and
> fine-tuning interfaces after you obtain the client through the Foundry
> project SDK. [Customize a model with fine-tuning](../../openai/how-to/fine-tuning.md)
rem: Fine-tuning lets you adapt a premium healthcare AI model to your data and domain tasks. This article covers prerequisites and steps to create a fine-tuning job, with links to the core fine-tuning workflow in Microsoft Foundry.
- A Foundry project in a region that supports your target fine-tuning model. If you don't have one, [create a project](../create-projects.md).

- Access to a [premium healthcare model](healthcare-ai-models.md) such as [MedImageInsight Premium (preview)](deploy-medimageinsight-premium.md) or [CxrReportGen Premium (preview)](deploy-cxrreportgen-premium.md) in the model catalog for your project.
- The **Foundry Owner** role, or a custom role that includes permissions to fine-tune and deploy models.
- Training and validation files in JSONL format, encoded as UTF-8 with BOM, and less than 512 MB per file.
- A healthcare data governance process that covers de-identification, retention, auditing, and access control.

> [!NOTE]

add: # Assign users and devices to traffic forwarding profiles

You can assign specific users, groups, devices, and device platforms to a Global Secure Access traffic forwarding profile. Assignments let you deploy a profile gradually and provide different traffic acquisition rules to different users and devices.
This article explains assignments for traffic forwarding profiles, including custom Private Access profiles.
To manage assignments, you must have:

- A [Global Secure Access Administrator](../identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference.md#global-secure-access-administrator) role in Microsoft Entra ID to view and manage the traffic forwarding profile.
- The required Global Secure Access product licenses. For details, see [What is Global Secure Access](overview-what-is-global-secure-access.md).
rem: # How to assign users and groups to traffic forwarding profiles

With the Global Secure Access traffic forwarding features, you can assign specific users and groups to a traffic forwarding profile. User or group assignment limits the scope of the traffic forwarding profile so you have a mechanism to roll out the profile safely and at a controlled pace.
This article describes how to assign specific users and groups to a traffic forwarding profile.
To assign a traffic forwarding profile to specific users and groups, you must have:

- A [Global Secure Access Administrator](../identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference.md#global-secure-access-administrator) role in Microsoft Entra ID to view the traffic forwarding profile.
- An [Application Administrator](../identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference.md#application-administrator) role to assign the traffic profile to the selected users and groups.

add: There are different roles, permissions, and license requirements to view health monitoring signals and to configure and receive alerts. We recommend using a role with least privilege access to align with the [Zero Trust guidance](/security/zero-trust/zero-trust-overview).
- A tenant with a [Microsoft Entra P1 or P2 license](/entra/fundamentals/get-started-premium) is required to *view* the Microsoft Entra health scenario monitoring signals.

- A tenant with a Microsoft Entra Global Secure Access license is required. For details, see the licensing section of [What is Global Secure Access?](/entra/global-secure-access/overview-what-is-global-secure-access).

- The [Reports Reader](/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference#reports-reader) role is the least privileged role required to *view scenario monitoring signals, alerts, and alert configurations*.

Account discovery retrieves users and groups from a target application and classifies them into three categories:

- **Local identities** — Users or groups in the target application that have no corresponding user or group in Microsoft Entra ID. These identities might belong to former employees, service accounts, users who were provisioned through a different process, groups created directly in the target applic

- **Unassigned identities** — Users or groups that match a user or group in Microsoft Entra ID but aren't assigned to the enterprise application. These identities exist in your directory but don't have the required application assignment for provisioning to manage them.

- **Assigned identities** — Users or groups that match a user or group in Microsoft Entra ID and are assigned to the enterprise application. These identities are fully managed by the provisioning service.
This classification gives you visibility into who has access to your applications and helps you identify identities that should be governed, reassigned, or removed.

watchlist.what: MC1474104, published 18 September, sets the date: from 1 February 2027 SMS first-factor sign-in is retired for Microsoft Entra ID workforce tenants worldwide and in GCC. Existing configurations stop being honoured and the management surface is removed.
watchlist.soc: Any account that can still sign in with a phone number and an SMS code is a phishable first factor with a February deadline on it. Inventory SignInNoPassword usage now; the population is usually frontline and shared-device users, who are the hardest to move.

watchlist.what: MC1426371, last revised 15 September, is the parent post: passkeys become the default registration path and Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication retire. Its own first deadline, 1 September 2026, has passed.
watchlist.soc: Tenants that relied on Microsoft-provided telephony have two exits — move to phishing-resistant methods, or bring their own telephony provider — and the provider route has its own dates.

watchlist.what: Provider information opened on 18 September 2026; customer configuration opens 30 October 2026, ahead of the February 2027 retirement.
watchlist.soc: This is the only path that keeps telephony-based methods alive. A tenant that wants it has roughly three months to select and contract a provider.

watchlist.topic: Passkeys as the first registered method
watchlist.what: MC1450133 lets a user register a passkey or another passwordless method as their first multifactor method, rather than having to register a phone first.
watchlist.soc: Removes the step that forced every new user through a phone number. It also removes the assumption, common in detection rules, that a first registration event is a phone registration.

watchlist.what: MC1459133 extends passkey registration and sign-in to B2B guest users in the resource tenant.
watchlist.soc: Guest identities have been the weakest link in phishing-resistant rollouts because the home tenant controlled the method. This gives the resource tenant a lever it did not have.

watchlist.topic: System-preferred authentication on the first factor
watchlist.what: System-preferred authentication starts applying to the first factor, not just to multifactor prompts, from 30 September 2026.
watchlist.soc: The method a user is offered first changes without any policy edit on the tenant side. Expect help-desk volume and a shift in the method distribution in sign-in logs at the end of the month.

watchlist.topic: AD FS DKM container ACL hardening
watchlist.what: MC1471963 is the 30-day reminder: the October 2026 Windows security update turns on Enforcement mode for AD FS Distributed Key Manager container ACL hardening, remediating insecure ACLs automatically to close CVE-2026-56155. Windows Server 2012 and 2012 R2 are not remediated automatically.
watchlist.soc: This writes to a Tier 0 object on the federation path. Use the remaining audit period to read the AD FS Admin event log and confirm nothing in the tenant depends on the loose ACL.

watchlist.what: MC1470871: Microsoft is removing user app role assignments and licence details from the delegated and application permission User.ReadBasic.All to fix a security vulnerability. Rollout began mid-September and is expected to complete late September 2026.
watchlist.soc: It is the permission people grant when they mean ‘read nothing sensitive’, and it has been returning app role assignments. Apps that legitimately need that data must move to User.Read.All or LicenseAssignment.Read.All before the rollout finishes.

kql.title: Apps that will break — or that quietly over-read — when User.ReadBasic.All stops returning app role assignments
kql.why: MC1470871 removes app role assignments and licence details from User.ReadBasic.All, completing late September 2026. Both questions matter: which apps break, and which have been reading assignment data they were never meant to see.
kql.query:
// Microsoft SOC Brief - 20 September 2026
// MC1470871: User.ReadBasic.All stops returning appRoleAssignments and licenseDetails.
// Find callers that hit those paths while holding only the basic scope.
// Table and columns: MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs -
// https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-monitor/reference/tables/microsoftgraphactivitylogs
MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where RequestUri has_any ("appRoleAssignments", "licenseDetails")
| extend Scope = tostring(Scopes), Role = tostring(Roles)
| extend BasicOnly = (Scope has "User.ReadBasic.All" or Role has "User.ReadBasic.All")
                     and not (Scope has "User.Read.All" or Role has "User.Read.All")
                     and not (Scope has "LicenseAssignment.Read.All"
                              or Role has "LicenseAssignment.Read.All")
| summarize Calls = count(),
            Breaking = countif(BasicOnly),
            LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated),
            Paths = make_set(RequestUri, 12),
            Statuses = make_set(ResponseStatusCode, 8)
        by AppId, ServicePrincipalId, Scope, Role
| where Breaking > 0
| sort by Breaking desc, Calls desc

kql.title: Which AD FS servers are still short of the July update before DKM ACL enforcement lands in October
kql.why: MC1471963 turns on Enforcement mode for AD FS DKM container ACL hardening with the October 2026 Windows security update, and the prerequisite is the 14 July 2026 update or later. A server behind that build gets remediated without the audit evidence.

kql.title: Devices still on the September rollup that the 14 September out-of-band update replaces
kql.why: MC1471876 released an out-of-band update on 14 September because the 8 September rollup could stop Remote Desktop Services responding, which blocks local and remote sign-in. A device stuck on the original build is one reboot away from losing its sign-in path.

actions.action: List every application holding NetworkAccess.ReadWrite.All and confirm each is still one you would grant it to today, now that it writes the Global Secure Access secure enterprise browser configuration. No consent prompt fired.

Check isAssignableToRole on every group that grants an Entra role. A group that is not role-assignable gives its eligible members no credential protection, so a Helpdesk or Authentication Administrator can reset their password and they can then elevate.

Re-cut the SMS and voice inventory into three populations — Global Administrators, external users, and everyone else including internal guests — and give each its own retirement date. Move the administrators first.

Add the six new Graph application roles to the consent-review list before the first grant request arrives, and decide now which of them may ever be consented. Treat AppCertTrustConfiguration.ReadWrite.All as privileged.
Disable Machine Identity Isolation by whichever channel enabled it on affected Windows 11 devices, restart, then run Test-ComputerSecureChannel -Repair. Microsoft's status is Mitigated, not Resolved.
Put a Conditional Access policy on the security information registration action requiring MFA or a trusted location, before passkey-as-first-method reaches general availability.

Decide the replacement for every Azure Blueprints lock — Azure Policy deny or denyAction for the rule, a resource lock for the deletion protection — and export every definition, version and assignment you intend to keep.
Author and validate EWSAllowedAppIDs yourself from the EWS usage report rather than inheriting the list Microsoft auto-generates from 60 days of observed traffic.
Deploy the single sign-on extension policy to iOS and iPadOS so just-in-time registration works, before web based enrollment becomes the default profile type.
Move insider-exfiltration correlation off the Purview data risk graph. Stop planning new Data Security Investigations configurations after 30 September.

strategic.head: Phone-based authentication is being dismantled on a published timetable
strategic.text: Between MC1426371, MC1474104 and the telephony-provider route, Microsoft has now dated every step of removing SMS and voice from Entra ID. Plan for a world where the only telephony left in the tenant is one the tenant pays for itself.

strategic.head: Permission scopes are being narrowed as security fixes, not as breaking changes
strategic.text: User.ReadBasic.All losing app role assignments is the second scope correction this quarter shipped under a security-fix banner. Treat any granted scope as a moving boundary and re-audit what it actually returns.

strategic.head: Tier 0 objects are being hardened by Windows Update rather than by admins
strategic.text: AD FS DKM container ACL remediation runs by default in October unless someone opts out. The pattern — a monthly update quietly rewriting directory permissions — will recur.

strategic.head: Message content is entering the hunting surface
strategic.text: The new MessageContents table puts Teams message snippets into advanced hunting. That is a genuine detection gain and a genuine privacy surface, and the access model has to be decided by the organisation rather than by whoever holds the query console.

strategic.head: Device attestation is moving to an Azure service
strategic.text: Intune's Windows Health Attestation migration to Microsoft Azure Attestation changes where the trust signal behind compliance comes from. Compliance policies that depend on it inherit a new dependency.

strategic.head: October is a lifecycle wall
strategic.text: Windows Server 2022 mainstream support, Windows 11 24H2 and Windows 10 LTSB 2016 updates, Office LTSC 2021 and Publisher all end on or around 13 October 2026. Everything competes for the same change window.

strategic.head: Microsoft's published permission surface and its live service no longer agree
strategic.text: The service principal carries 982 scopes against 997 documented names, and the deployment map carries names that appear in neither. The gap is not an error to reconcile; it is the earliest signal this brief gets.

strategic.head: The Learn what's new feeds keep running behind Message Center
strategic.text: Entra's consolidated feed is still showing June 2026 as its newest month. For identity, Message Center is the primary source and the documentation is the confirmation, not the other way round.

apis.name: Microsoft Purview
apis.description: Microsoft Purview data-plane REST APIs — catalog, scanning, account, metadata policy and DevOps policy planes, reached with a token for https://purview.azure.net.
apis.socNote: Read on 1 Sep 2026, on its due date. The Microsoft Purview data plane takes a token for the resource https://purview.azure.net and Microsoft documents NO named delegated or application permission for it: authorisation is decided entirely by Purview's own data-plane roles — Data Curator, Data Source Administrator, Collection Admin, Policy Author. For a SOC this is the finding, not an empty result: an app-consent review of this surface will show nothing, because the grant that matters is a Purview role assignment and it never appears in Entra consent reporting. Zero is a read, not a gap.

Invisible in any Graph permission report.

roles.name: External Identity Provider Administrator
roles.description: Can configure identity providers for use in direct federation.
roles.intro: This is a privileged role. This administrator manages federation between Microsoft Entra organizations and external identity providers. With this role, users can add new identity providers and configure all available settings (e.g. authentication path, service ID, assigned key containers). This user can enable the Microsoft Entra organization to trust authentications from external identity providers. The resulting impact on end-user experiences depends on the type of organization:
tasks: Microsoft Entra organizations for employees and partners: The addition of a federation (e.g. with Gmail) will immediately impact all guest invitations not yet redeemed. See Adding Google as an identity provider for B2B guest users.

Azure Active Directory B2C organizations: The addition of a federation (for example, with Facebook, or with another Microsoft Entra organization) does not immediately impact end-user flows until the identity provider is added as an option in a user flow (also called a built-in policy). See Configuring a Microsoft account as an identity provider for an example. To change user flows, the limited role of "B2C User Flow Administrator" is required.
